Robust day-ahead self-scheduling of concentrating solar power plants under correlated uncertainty
A field-scale model for simulating the redistribution of solar radiation and water on the ground surface under solar panels in agrivoltaic systems
Investigation of the photothermal–electrical characteristics of insulated and ventilated photovoltaic vacuum glazing systems

Analysis of the operational characteristics and control strategies on a novel CHP system co-driven by solar, wind, and natural gas with the coordination of renewable energy priority consumption and energy storage
Efficiency of cellulosic ethanol production by Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Mucor indicus from biomass after microwave-assisted pretreatment with aqueous solutions of deep eutectic solvents
abstract: Current trends promote a reduction of the quantity of chemicals used and resorting to energy-effective methods of heating biomass. This study aims to assess the usefulness of microwave radiation and selected aqueous solutions of deep eutectic solvents in preparing oat hull or brewer’s spent grain biomass for the production of cellulosic ethanol. Fermentation was carried out using the Saccharomyces cerevisiae or Mucor indicus . Oat hull pretreatment using an aqueous solution of choline chloride and ethylene glycol led to the generation of biomass highly susceptible to enzymatic degradation. The above resulted in hydrolysates containing 116.8 g/L of glucose, which constituted complementary fermentation media for yeast ( S. cerevisiae) enabling comprehensive attenuation within 48 hours and the generation of ethanol concentration at 54.5 g/L. The use of S. cerevisiae resulted in a faster conversion of glucose to ethanol in comparison with M. indicus , regardless of the plant biomass type. Additionally, the acquired lignocellulosic hydrolysates, after supplementation with amino nitrogen compounds, constituted a medium facilitating an effective production of M. indicus biomass under oxygen conditions. Tests clearly indicate the possibility of using the developed pretreatment method in the cellulosic ethanol production.

title: Modelling hot water and power production from a low-enthalpy geothermal carbonate reservoir; South Swan Hills, Alberta, Canada
abstract: South Swan Hills field co-produces oil, gas and 700 – 1100 m3 of >100ºC water daily from a Devonian carbonate reef in the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin, creating an opportunity for geothermal electrical power generation. We apply field data for flow modelling and estimation of geothermal reserves. A reservoir model comprises three regions: reef interior (non-reservoir); reef margin forming a continuous 1 – 2 km wide zone of high quality grainstones; and terminal shoal, 10 – 15 m thick, with reservoir and non-reservoir elements. Reservoir porosity ranges from 3.20% to 14.5% and permeability from 0.21 to 73.0 mD (P10 to P90).Flow simulations with well doublets identify an optimal spacing of 400 to 500 meters; more closely spaced wells display rapid cold plume invasion, while wells spaced >500m have poor pressure connectivity. Varying porosity and permeability values captures uncertainty in reservoir performance and power production. Thermal power production estimates ranged from 32.8 – 2.73 x 103 kW per doublet in the shoal and from 64.6 – 3.20 x 103 kW in the reef margin. In-situ thermal potential is estimated at 8.46 – 12.8 MW in the reef margin and 4.17 – 16.4 MW in the terminal shoal over 25 years.

title: Decarbonization potential of district heating systems using deep coaxial borehole heat exchangers in salt dome geological settings
abstract: The decarbonization of district heating systems remains a major challenge in Central and Eastern Europe, where high-temperature networks are still largely supplied by coal-fired plants. This study evaluates the technical potential of integrating a deep coaxial borehole heat exchanger (DCBHE) into the HOCLOOP ( HO rizontal C losed LOOP ) concept, which considers a vertical depth of 3690 m and a horizontal section length of 2500 m for the borehole heat exchanger coupled with an existing 2nd generation district heating system. Based on numerical simulations, the share of renewable energy during system operation was quantified. A case study of the Goleniów city district heating network in SW Poland is analyzed using long-term numerical simulations of a DCBHE installed in a high-conductivity salt formation, coupled with time-resolved heat demand based on typical meteorological year data (TMY). Two integration pathways are assessed: direct low-temperature heat recovery and cooperation with large-scale heat pumps. Results over a 20-year period indicate stable thermal performance, with outlet temperatures exceeding 80–100°C depending on the circulation rate and operating mode. Integration with heat pumps enables multi-megawatt thermal output and substantial reductions in coal use and CO 2 emissions. While geothermal energy alone cannot exceed a 50% share of renewables in the existing Goleniów system due to high power and supply-temperature requirements (∼20.5 MW, 135°C). If one considers a hypothetical scenario, analyses suitably matched users, as assumed in the paper, of approximately 8 MW for central heating and 530 kW for hot tap water, and 3rd-generation DH – requiring a supply temperature of 90°C – can achieve renewable energy shares above 50% using even a single unit of DCBHE combined with a heat pump. This indicates that matching the source's capabilities to the recipient's requirements is a key aspect of achieving good system efficiency. A 50% share of renewable energy sources is important for classifying the system as energy-efficient under the Energy Efficiency Directive (EED). The results demonstrate that long-term near-full energy self-sufficiency (∼0.92 share of RES) can also be achieved for a 3rd-generation DH system with a total power demand of ∼3.2 MW, assuming a single DCBHE module of design. It was estimated that the simple payback period for DBBHE expenditures is about 36-40 years, and the total energy cost is ∼32-38 €/GJ, similar to that for conventional energy carriers, assuming a 4.7%/year inflation in energy carrier prices.

title: Optimization of photosynthetic biogas upgrading in a demo-scale algal-bacterial photobioreactor
abstract: A demo-scale system consisting of an 82 m 3 high-rate algal pond (HRAP) coupled with a 0.5 m 3 absorption column was operated for 710 days to photosynthetically upgrade biogas generated from the anaerobic digestion of municipal solid waste. Operation began with nutrient supplementation and was progressively adapted to enable a microalgal–bacterial consortium to utilize raw digestate as the sole nutrient source. The liquid-to-gas (L/G) ratio in the absorption column was dynamically adjusted in response to variations in biogas composition. Removal of hydrogen sulphide (H 2 S) was consistently >99%, even under substantial fluctuations in inlet concentrations. Average carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) removal over the entire operational period was 90 ± 15%, increasing to values of up to 98% after day 660, coinciding with a more stable biogas flowrate and an enhanced gas composition. Biomass harvesting strategies were implemented to maintain algal concentrations between 1.0 and 2.5 g L -1 , supporting process stability. Overall, this study demonstrates the long-term feasibility and robustness of a demo-scale HRAP–absorption column system for biogas upgrading, with additional benefits of nutrient recycling from digestate, reduced dependency on external inputs, and improved economic and environmental sustainability. The results provide valuable operational data to support the industrial scale-up of this integrated technology.

title: Microwave assisted hydrothermal pretreatment of arecanut husk with anaerobic spent media for biohydrogen production using mono and coculture of microorganisms
Experimental study on dust removal of linear Fresnel reflectors based on rainfall and compressed air
Microalgae-based sustainable aviation fuel: Kinetic framework, process simulation, and fuel property analysis
Comparative assessment of magnetic pretreatment across low to moderate intensities for enhancing anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge
abstract: This study investigates the effect of static magnetic field (SMF) pretreatment at different field intensities on the anaerobic digestion (AD) of sewage sludge. Three SMF intensities (10, 20, and 50 mT) were applied through tubular magnetic polarizers under varying numbers of magnetization cycles (NMC) to assess their impact on biomethane production. The 20 mT condition with a single NMC yielded the highest improvement, increasing methane production by 21% compared to the untreated sludge. Lower (10 mT) and higher (50 mT) intensities produced modest enhancements, suggesting a nonlinear correlation between SMF strength and methane generation. Volatile fatty acid analysis indicated that pretreatment at 20 mT enhanced hydrolysis and acidogenesis. Microbial investigation further showed that moderate SMF exposure reshaped the sludge community, enriching fermentative and syntrophic taxa that promote organic matter degradation and efficient methanogenesis. Unlike energy-intensive pretreatments, the proposed SMF system operates passively, using permanent magnets to generate magnetic exposure without external power input. Preliminary economic analysis suggests that this energy-neutral approach can lower sludge management costs while improving overall energy recovery.

title: Enhancing methane production from waste activated sludge via iron-mediated low-temperature thermal hydrolysis
Design and experimental validation of a novel asymmetric airfoil turbine with mechanical rectification for OWC systems: A comparison with an impulse turbine
Parametric experimental investigation of a floating pneumatic wave energy converter with forward and backward bent ducts
Performance evaluation and multi-objective optimization of a building powered by photovoltaic-thermal and air source heat pump heating system
abstract: Photovoltaic-thermal and air source heat pump (PV/T-ASHP) heating system constitutes a significant technological approach for building energy conservation and carbon emission reduction. The structural parameters of PV/T modules are critical to their power generation performance，and require integrated design based on application scenarios. This study established a TRNSYS-MATLAB co-simulation model based on an office building in Lanzhou New Area. It analyzed the effects of number of tubes and absorber plate thickness in PV/T modules on electricity generation and heating supply within a heating system under different absorber plate materials. The results demonstrated that aluminum was the optimal absorber plate material for PV/T modules in the heating system. In the optimized heating system, increasing the number of heat exchange tubes had a greater impact on system performance than increasing the absorber plate thickness. Compared with the air source heat pump heating system, the optimized heating system exhibited lower operating costs after 5.08 years. This study obtained a result in terms of both energy and economics, providing a reference for performance-enhanced system design.

title: Determination of optimal locations for utility-scale photovoltaic installations in Turkiye for improved performance and service lifetime
Multiscale root mean square for hydropower generation systems: a scalable feature extraction method for condition-based maintenance
A super-Gaussian theoretical model to calculate the near wake velocity distribution of wind turbine
Unraveling spatial multi-scale energy loss mechanisms in a large Francis turbine: a mean kinetic energy perspective
Real-time hybrid testing of rotor control for a 15 MW floating wind turbine: platform pitch mitigation and rotor-speed stabilisation
abstract: Control strategies incorporating platform motion feedback have been developed and demonstrated via hydro-aero-servo-modelling for floating wind turbines to mitigate platform pitch motion and rotor speed variation, thereby improving system reliability and maintainability. The gain-scheduling floating feedback approach has shown distinct advantages over land-based and constant-gain control strategies in mitigating negative aerodynamic damping and reducing rotor speed variation above rated wind speed. Here we demonstrate its efficacy in a hybrid physical system, where the hydrodynamics is modelled physically (with Froude scaling) and the aerodynamics in turbulent wind under rotor control is simulated via the in-house aero-servo solver OREGEN_BEMT. The platform motion is measured optically and fed into the control algorithms in real time. The unsteady turbine thrust is replicated by a thruster at hub height, comprising two drone propellers. The experiments show that platform pitch motions near rated wind speed are markedly reduced by the gain-scheduling approach incorporating floating feedback, with the standard deviation roughly 50% lower than that of conventional land-based control. The rotor speed standard deviation is reduced by approximately 20%, accompanied by a slight increase in mean generator power and slightly reduced variability. This reduction in platform pitch motion is consistent with wind-only tests, indicating that the steep nonlinear waves tested do not impair control performance. Since blade pitch and generator torque variations within appropriate constraints are quite standard, the approach is effectively cost-free and easy to implement. This hybrid testing lends confidence to the practical applicability of the approach.

title: Co-production of biodiesel and hydrogen from microalgae biomass: Process technology and life cycle assessment
Energy harvesting and motion reduction using linear generators on small ships
abstract: In this study, we assess the potential for generating power from the wave-induced motions of a ship by using a linear generator to convert the ship's reciprocating motion into electrical energy. Rather than focusing on the numerous practical details, this preliminary study uses simulations to investigate the overall potential of the concept, and we present a simplified yet physically consistent assessment framework that explicitly accounts for the dynamic coupling between ship motions and the generator’s seismic mass. The numerical investigations are focused on boats of lengths 8-10 m, where the relatively large seismic mass in the generator leads to strong coupling between the wave-induced boat motions and the (relative) motion of the seismic mass. We show that for a weight ratio, seismic mass to boat mass, of around 10\%, auxiliary power generation up to 3-5 kW appears realistic for sailing in modest sea states with wave heights of 1-1.5 m. In addition, energy extraction from the wave-ship system can lead to considerable reduction of the boat's motion, up to about 25\% considering the vertical motion in the bow region. This, in turn, reduces the added resistance in waves by up to 15\% for the studied cases.

title: Research on the heat storage characteristics of building envelope structures for heating with photovoltaic power
A flexible and secure model predictive control strategy for frequency regulation of wind turbines considering fatigue load mitigation
Comparison between thermophilic-mesophilic two-phase and thermophilic single-phase process in anaerobic digestion of rice straw: Biomethane production, energy balance and microbial structure
abstract: To fill the research gap in two-phase anaerobic digestion (TPAD) of rice straw, this study assessed the performance of a thermophilic–mesophilic TPAD system over 180 days in terms of methane production, energy balance, and microbial community structure and compared it with a thermophilic single-phase anaerobic digestion (SPAD) system. Results showed that SPAD achieved a methane yield of 170 ± 14 mL CH 4 /g-VS, with VS and cellulose removal efficiencies of 39.8% and 59.5%, respectively. In contrast, TPAD produced 101 ± 8 mL CH 4 /g-VS and achieved 36.9% and 49.1% removal of VS and cellulose. The lower CH 4 conversion in TPAD might be caused by the mismatch between the recalcitrant structure of rice straw and conventional temperature configurations in two-phase process. The economic assessment suggested that although TPAD reduced the net energy deficit by 56% compared with SPAD, both configurations operated with negative net energy balance. Microbial analysis further revealed that community structure and functional characteristics were strongly shaped by process configuration. This study will provide some guidance for future optimization of lignocellulosic biomass valorization.

title: Geo-THM characterization for safe CO2 storage and geothermal energy in karstified-fractured carbonates: A reservoir and geomechanical risk management framework
Where incentives hit the roof: How policy design shapes rooftop solar returns
Effects of water washing and acid leaching on the thermochemical characteristics of canola straw for solid biofuel pellet production
abstract: Canola straw is a promising biofuel feedstock; however, its high ash content and alkali metals lead to severe slagging, fouling, and operational challenges during thermochemical conversion. In this study, ultrapure deionized (DI) water and multiple acidic solvents, including acetic, citric, phosphoric, hydrochloric, sulfuric, and nitric acids, were systematically evaluated for washing and leaching to enhance fuel quality. Among the tested treatments, DI water, 1 M acetic acid, 99.7 wt% acetic acid, and 1 M hydrochloric acid significantly improved energy density, carbon content, and combustion behavior. Optimal conditions were identified at liquid-to-solid ratios of 74 and 50 L kg −1 and a leaching duration of 3 h at 60 °C, reducing ash content from 3.2% to 1.1% with DI water and to 0.5% with 1 M acetic acid. DI water effectively removed soluble inorganic species, including Na (73.1%), K (84.8%), P (77.5%), and S (76.4%), while 1 M acetic acid achieved greater than 99% removal of major ash-forming elements. These reductions translated into markedly improved ash behavior, with decreased slagging, fouling, and agglomeration tendencies and enhanced ash stability. The results demonstrate that mild organic acid leaching, particularly with acetic acid, is a highly effective and scalable strategy for upgrading canola straw into a cleaner and more efficient solid biofuel.

title: Transient thermal performance of U-loop geothermal systems with dual-borehole lateral sections using a computationally efficient framework
abstract: Advancements in directional drilling technologies have facilitated the development of advanced geothermal system configurations at greater subsurface depths. One example is the enhanced U-loop geothermal configuration demonstrated in a pilot field study in Alberta, Canada, featuring dual lateral boreholes in the horizontal section. This study develops a transient numerical model of a conjugate ground–wellbore system representing a U-loop geothermal configuration with dual lateral sections, incorporating the superposition principle to account for thermal interactions between the boreholes. The model is validated against 516 days of field data from the Alberta pilot demonstration, achieving a maximum error of 4.5% in predicting outlet water temperature. Two geothermal system designs are evaluated with installation depths of 2.4 km and 7 km, corresponding to bottomhole temperatures of 78 °C and 221 °C, respectively. The effect of single- and dual-lateral configurations is investigated, showing that the modified design extracts about 110% more thermal power on average. A thermal to electricity conversion analysis shows that the enhanced configuration delivers geothermal water at 155 °C to the power plant inlet, resulting in 57% greater electricity generation potential than the conventional U-loop configuration under the same operating conditions. A techno-economic analysis shows that, although the additional lateral borehole increases drilling costs by 14.5%, the levelized cost of energy is reduced by 28.5% compared to the conventional U-loop configuration. A series of parametric studies on operational conditions further demonstrates that extending casing insulation length can mitigate 2.9–7 °C/km temperature loss during upward circulation at low flow rates associated with longer fluid residence times. Overall, this study provides key insights into the long-term design, optimization, and techno-economic performance of enhanced U-loop geothermal systems for integrated electricity generation and direct-use heating applications.

title: Improving the realism of hydropower and hydropower–battery hybrid plant optimization: A forecast-aware rolling horizon model
Fabrication of bimetallic hierarchical Cu-O-Zn@ZSM-5 assisting from ZIFs for selective catalytic cracking of WCOHAV to long-chain alkanes
How renewable energy mix shapes day-ahead price predictability: A comparative analysis of solar, wind, and biomass in Czechia
abstract: Understanding how renewable energy mixes influence day-ahead electricity price predictability is essential for market operations and renewable integration in thermally dominated systems. This study analyzes one year of hourly data from the Czech electricity market. Five forecasting models are evaluated across four renewable-dominance regimes. Solar-dominated hours yield the lowest forecasting errors, with Random Forest achieving an RMSE of 10.97 euros per megawatt hour, reflecting the regular diurnal alignment of solar generation with load. Fossil-dominated hours exhibit the highest errors, with an RMSE of 48.53 euros per megawatt hour and frequent extreme price spikes. Biomass contributes modest stabilizing effects, while wind plays a minimal role in price formation. SHAP analysis on the top-performing Random Forest model shows that higher solar and overall renewable shares reduce the sensitivity of prices to imports and load, alongside persistent lagged-price effects. Seasonal and weekly error patterns confirm that predictability improves when renewable output aligns with demand. The mechanisms identified are applicable to similar thermally dominated, interconnected power systems beyond Czechia. The findings indicate that expanding solar and biomass capacity can stabilize day-ahead prices in flexible thermal systems and support regime-aware forecasting strategies for Central European market operators.

title: Performance, response surface, energy, exergy and economic analyses of a biomass engine-thermoelectric-thermosyphon hybrid system for sustainable power generation via waste heat recovery
Green hydrogen energy storage to support microgrid Arctic communities on the pathway to 100% renewable energy
abstract: Remote Arctic communities in Canada face significant challenges in transitioning from diesel-dependent energy systems to renewable alternatives. While wind, solar, and battery technologies enable renewable energy penetration (REP) up to approximately 60%, exceeding this level requires long-duration energy storage. This study evaluates the potential of green hydrogen energy storage to support Arctic microgrids on the pathway to 100% REP using an optimization model and a community case study. This evaluated the least-cost designs for REP targets from 50% to 100%, comparing scenarios with and without hydrogen energy storage. The analysis incorporated operational constraints including minimum load ratio, ramping limitations, and compression requirements, as well as a cost sensitivity analysis. Results demonstrate that hydrogen energy storage becomes economically attractive above 65% REP, providing substantial cost savings at high REP by reducing renewable generation over-sizing requirements. However, technological limitations, particularly minimum loading of fuel cells, prevent cost-effective achievement of 100% REP. Beyond economic benefits, the study identifies practical implementation challenges including harsh environmental conditions, logistical constraints, and local capacity. This work provides novel insights into hydrogen's potential role in Arctic microgrid decarbonization and identifies key technological and practical barriers that must be addressed for successful its implementation.

title: Assessing policy strategies for residential solar photovoltaic adoption: A system dynamics approach with heuristic optimization
A hybrid intelligent approach for university building energy management: Integrating GABP prediction with improved PSO scheduling
Synergistic effects of enriched inoculum and headspace pressure on acidogenesis and its effect on methane yield in two-stage anaerobic digestion of food waste
abstract: Regulation of in situ hydrogen partial pressure enhances hydrolysis efficiency and reduces hydraulic retention time during the acidogenic phase of kitchen waste digestion. High-solids anaerobic digestion systems (> 20% total solids) require a comprehensive understanding of acidogenic microorganisms that can withstand dynamic headspace pressures and varying substrate compositions. This research explores a two-stage digestion process incorporating an enriched inoculum with pressure-assisted hydrolysis in a leach bed reactor (LBR) linked to an up-flow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB) reactor to optimize energy recovery from kitchen waste (KW). The KW was mixed with the enriched inoculum and digested in LBRs under controlled headspace pressures of 3 psi (20.7 kPa) and 12 psi (82.7 kPa), using pre-mixed biogas (CH 4 :CO 2 = 60:40). The system operated at 12 psi exhibited elevated levels of soluble chemical oxygen demand (sCOD: 559.2 g/kg VS) and total soluble products (TSP: 362 g/kg VS) compared to the 3 psi condition (sCOD: 425.1 g/kg VS; TSP: 294 g/kg VS). Microbial community analysis revealed pressure-driven shifts favouring Pseudomonas , Escherichia , and Clostridium species. Metabolite profiling indicated butyrate dominance at 12 psi, while propionate concentrations were higher at 3 psi. Methane yield in the UASB reactor paired with the 12 psi LBR (421.8 L/kg VS) was higher relative to the 3-psi setup (310.1 L/kg VS). These findings underscore the effectiveness of combining tailored microbial consortia with pressure and gas composition control to enhance intermediate metabolite conversion and overall bioenergy output in high-solids anaerobic digestion systems.

title: Optical design and crop-light planning for photovoltaic greenhouses under fixed and sun-tracking panel configurations
abstract: Agrivoltaic greenhouses offer a pathway to combine renewable electricity generation with protected crop production, yet photovoltaic roof integration can substantially reduce and redistribute crop-available light. This study introduces an integrated ray-tracing-to-analytics workflow for quantifying how photovoltaic layout and actuation shape the spatiotemporal light environment in a polytunnel greenhouse. Seven photovoltaic configurations and a no-panel reference were evaluated over a seasonal cycle using real-weather boundary conditions, 15-minute simulations, and a dense canopy-level sensor grid. The tested designs varied module width, row density, and operating mode, comparing fixed layouts with single-axis sun-tracking systems. Photovoltaic integration reduced mean canopy irradiance from 379.5 W m -2 in the no-panel reference to 289.8-315.0 W m -2 , corresponding to a 17-24% reduction depending on configuration. Although tracking altered shading dynamics, it did not improve the seasonal average canopy light. Instead, fixed layouts produced approximately 15-19% lower spatial variability than comparable tracking layouts, indicating more stable light distribution at similar mean irradiance. To translate optical simulations into design guidance, a multi-objective ranking framework was developed to compare light retention and spatial uniformity across scenarios. Monthly light-availability estimates further distinguished open and under-panel growing zones, with under-panel areas receiving approximately 70-80% of open-zone light availability. Hereinafter, the results show that photovoltaic density, module width, and actuation strategy strongly govern crop-relevant light conditions. The proposed workflow provides quantitative support for selecting greenhouse photovoltaic layouts that balance energy integration with spatially uniform crop light availability.

title: Inferring wind-energy inflow spectra from height and stability: A cumulative-energy log-normal model with operator-learned compensation
A tool for economic assessment of investment decisions for multi-energy systems
abstract: Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) enable collective participation in local renewable generation, storage, distribution and consumption. However, optimal design is shaped by electricity settlement and compensation schemes. These regulatory mechanisms are often represented exogenously in planning tools, limiting transparent comparison of transition pathways. This paper presents a regulation-aware planning tool based on an integrated optimisation framework for community-scale energy systems. Electricity settlement and compensation rules for local self-consumption schemes are embedded within a mixed-integer linear model, with photovoltaic (PV) generation considered as primary application. The framework enables techno-economic assessment of individual and collective investment configurations under net billing (NB), net metering (NM) and feed-in tariff (FiT) schemes, with monthly and annual settlement horizons. Electricity system optimisation is coupled with low-carbon heat supply options, including biomass-based cogeneration and individual heat pumps. The framework is applied to a real-world case in Ispaster (Spain). Results show that regulatory design and aggregation level drive optimal sizing and economic performance. Collective configurations and annual settlement consistently outperform individual and monthly alternatives, while battery storage adds limited value once annual settlement is available. The proposed approach supports community-level planning and investment decisions through regulation-aware comparison of alternative energy transition options.

title: Reducing the number of wind turbine prototype measurement campaigns for power curve model validation using a model-validity predictor
abstract: Prototype turbine measurement campaigns are required for turbine type certification and the associated validation of aero-elastic wind turbine models when wind turbine designs slightly differ from previous measurement campaigns. Small changes in the turbine design are allowed without additional testing campaigns being required. We propose a model-validity predictor that is able to conservatively predict the validation results on new turbines before a measurement campaign is carried out. This predictor is trained based on previous measurement campaigns and uses a set of variables to describe the wind turbine design space. The model-validity predictor demonstrates the potential to reduce the number of prototype campaigns required to validate a model, and it is shown that a change of variables can expand the predicted safe domain by 72%. Detailed uncertainty propagation is carried out for each wind turbine measurement campaign using Monte Carlo simulations. We separate aleatoric uncertainties and parameter epistemic uncertainties. This separation enables us to quantify the degree of validity of a model with respect to the measurements. This study demonstrates the potential benefits of calibration, with the qualification that the ideal workflow will separate data used for validation and calibration, perhaps using a sophisticated cross-validation routine.

title: Method based on optimized tendencies to evaluate the impact of the introduction of solar and wind energy sources in energy systems
abstract: Fossil fuels continue to dominate global energy use but are a major source of GHG-emissions driving climate change. This makes the transition to clean, carbon-free energy sources increasingly urgent. The introduction of solar and wind sources is an essential step toward decarbonization not only because their costs are steadily falling but also because they are among the most widely available local energy resources in many regions around the world. However, these energy sources cannot always meet demand, as their production depends on the intensity of solar radiation and wind. Due to this intermittency, they must be supplemented by energy storage systems or/and by conventional, controllable sources that can adjust their output to follow fluctuations in demand. The characteristics of the backup energy needed to compensate for the intermittency of solar and wind energy vary considerably depending on the share of these sources in the grid, both in terms of average load and peak load. This article analyses how these shifting needs impact the cost and distribution of generation technologies, especially in systems that lack energy storage. It presents the development of a method capable of accounting for this while managing many scenarios of increasing introduction of intermittent energy into the mix, and several indicators of interest for stakeholders are needed. The energy mix for each scenario is determined by minimizing energy production costs. Two regions—Grand-Est in France and Cuba—are examined.

title: Improved modeling, parametric analysis, and experimental validation of freestanding rotary electret nanogenerator
Effect of alkali metals on gasification reaction characteristics of pine sawdust and kinetic analysis in dielectric barrier discharge
Preliminary investigations on the evacuated PVT-driven methanol electrolysis for enhanced solar hydrogen production
Novel hydrogen fuel cell vehicle-to-grid strategy for peak shaving in renewable-powered residential microgrids
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in residential microgrids introduces challenges for peak load management and grid stability. Hydrogen-powered fuel cell electric vehicles offer a promising solution by combining mobility with distributed energy storage. This study investigates vehicle-to-grid operation of hydrogen fuel cell vehicles that can efficiently alleviate short-term peak demand occurrences, providing targeted flexibility and reinforcing microgrid resilience. A Matlab/Simulink simulation model of a residential microgrid with 6.5 MW of solar power and 4.5 MW of wind turbines was developed, considering a fleet of 15 vehicles. Results demonstrate a peak load reduction capability of 100%, with the entire fleet delivering 484 kWh, with a peak of 520 kW, in 95 minutes, while the hydrogen utilization ratio varied between 21% and 37%. The paper demonstrates that fuel cell vehicle fleet can fully eliminate overloads, confirming the potential role of hydrogen-based mobility in enhancing renewable-powered microgrids.

title: Solar-assisted heating of a medium-deep U-type borehole heat exchanger system: Improved operational performance and mitigated subsurface thermal attenuation
LLM-CECM: A simulation framework for strategic generation behavior in coupled electricity-carbon markets
abstract: The deep integration of electricity and carbon markets creates a coupled decision environment in which generators must coordinate energy offers, quota positions, and expectations about policy shocks. Traditional market simulators often either simplify strategic cognition or incur prohibitive computational cost when richer reasoning is introduced. This paper proposes LLM-CECM, a rolling multi-agent simulation framework in which carbon-order submission, carbon-cost feedback, and electricity dispatch interact at every time step. The framework combines: (1) LLM-enabled agents with persona, memory, and belief modules; (2) an Adaptive Decision Frequency (ADF) mechanism that allocates expensive reasoning only to informative periods; and (3) a fixed-depth Iterated Belief Revision with Counterfactual Reasoning (IBR-CR) heuristic for anticipating rival responses. In the reported IEEE 118-bus/AEMO-based experiments, ADF reduces LLM calls by 80.5% and runtime by 81.5%, while IBR-CR lowers the rolling price-volatility proxy from 5.49 to 2.69 CNY/MWh. Event-window diagnostics further show that thermal agents increase markups and quota purchases during a pre-announced multi-event stress sequence involving demand tightening, coal outages, and later renewable relief. These results should be interpreted as empirical evidence from a rolling simulation framework rather than a proof of equilibrium existence, uniqueness, or Nash convergence in the underlying coupled market game.

title: Transformer prediction decomposition dual-driver for maximum power point tracking under partial shading conditions of photovoltaic power generation systems

Modeling and coordinated control optimization of the focused flux distribution for a discrete solar-simulator concentrator
Synergistic parametric optimisation of gas–liquid interaction with valve lift and liquid column in an ionic liquid hydrogen compressor
Reducing market risk in run-of-river hydropower: The economic value of improving predictions of day-ahead production
abstract: Accurate streamflow forecasts are essential for optimizing hydropower production and reducing market imbalance costs, particularly for small-scale hydropower plants with limited storage capacity. This study evaluates the potential of an LSTM neural network for hourly streamflow prediction at operationally monitored hydropower systems with limited historical observations and assesses its economic value in a hydropower production context. The effect of two aspects on prediction accuracy is investigated: (i) including back-calculated streamflow data from 110 run-of-river hydropower plants during training, and (ii) implementation of a data assimilation (DA) approach using back-calculated streamflow as input. The performance of the model is assessed in a perfect weather forecast context using regional reanalysis data and compared with both a persistence model and the operational model currently used by the largest small-scale hydropower operator in the Nordics, Småkraft AS. The results show that including data from hydropower plants in training provides the model with valuable information, while data assimilation yields the greatest performance gain. The proposed model has the potential to decrease annual imbalance fees for Småkraft AS by 23.6% (143 kEUR) compared to the model currently used and reduces exposure to extreme prices in the balancing market by reducing the CVaR 75 with 16% (380 kEUR). The findings demonstrate that enhanced hydrological forecasting reduces imbalance cost and market risk, while supporting more stable grid operations.

title: Performance enhancement of concentrated photovoltaic/thermal systems using water cooling and phase change materials under outdoor conditions
A novel distributed model predictive control-based optimal energy management of islanded multimicrogrids with renewable energies and hybrid storage
Thermal depletion patterns of CO2 and water in closed-loop coaxial geothermal systems with vertical and L-shaped wells
Experimental performance of solar-assisted water source heat pump system coupled with convection-radiation terminals: operational behaviors and energy-saving potentials
Field investigation of diurnal boundary layer effects on wind farm wake evolution and power performance
Feasibility of boosting single-step biohydrogen production from sugarcane bagasse mediated by RSBA-biochar
Low-Carbon Operation Mode of the wind-photovoltaic-thermal-hydro-pumped storage hydropower combined generation system
abstract: Pumped storage hydropower plants (PSHP) have emerged as a fundamental component in the consumption of wind and photovoltaic(PV) resources and the reduction of carbon emissions. To address the challenge of coordinating PSHP with wind, PV, cascade hydropower, and thermal power plants, multiple PSHP scenarios are established to quantify the carbon reduction effect and the differences in reducing residual load fluctuations. A coordinated optimization model combined wind, PV, hydropower, PSHP, and thermal power plants is constructed, and the life cycle assessment (LCA) methodology is used to quantify the carbon emissions. Multiple operation scenarios are established by considering seasonal variations in the residual load, operating modes of PSHP, and dispatch objectives. By comparing the differences in carbon emission reductions and residual load fluctuations across various scenarios, an optimal operating mode for PSHP is declared. Results indicated that after incorporating carbon reduction into objectives, the carbon emissions decreased by 6.3% to 22.6% while maintaining overall output. It means that low-carbon energy replaces high-carbon energy. The output and water level changes indicate that the coordinated operation effects of the combined generation system are related to the reservoir's reserved storage capacity, residual load process, available water volume, number of pump-discharge cycles, and duration of pump-discharge flow. For scenarios characterized by multiple peaks in residual load with significant variations and limited available water volume, the one-pump and one-discharge operation mode is adopted. Conversely, for scenarios where residual load peaks show minimal variation and sufficient water volume, the one-pump and two-discharge scheduling mode is more appropriate.

title: Editorial Board
Framework for circular economy strategies in wind turbine end-of-life management
abstract: This study develops an integrated decision-support framework to evaluate circular economy (CE) strategies for wind turbine generator (WTG) end-of-life management. The proposed framework combines economic, environmental, and circularity indicators to assess alternative pathways including repair, refurbishment, reuse, remanufacturing, recycling, and repowering. A circularity metric based on the 9R framework is introduced to quantify the relative circular performance of different scenarios. Through scenario-based analysis, the framework evaluates the impacts of lifetime extension strategies on annual energy yield, emissions savings, and economic performance. The results highlight the significant potential of second-hand WTG markets, particularly under favorable wind conditions at new installation sites. The findings further demonstrate that increased circularity can simultaneously improve resource efficiency, reduce environmental impacts, and create additional economic value. The proposed framework provides a transparent and adaptable tool to support decision-making toward more sustainable and circular practices in the wind energy sector.

title: Ultra-short-term PV power forecasting under complex sky conditions using all-sky imaging and physically informed dynamic features
Study on wellbore flow and heat transfer characteristics in a surface-well-reservoir coupled compressed CO2 energy storage system
Pyrolysis-catalytic steam reforming of sewage sludge for the production of hydrogen/syngas over Ni-Fe/Al2O3 bimetallic catalysts prepared by the redox method
A model predictive control approach to dual-axis agrivoltaic panel tracking
abstract: Agrivoltaic systems--photovoltaic (PV) panels installed above agricultural land--have emerged as a promising dual-use solution to address competing land demands for food and energy production. In this paper, we propose a model predictive control (MPC) approach to dual-axis agrivoltaic panel tracking control that dynamically adjusts panel positions in real time to maximize power production and crop yield given solar irradiance and ambient temperature measurements. We apply convex relaxations and shading factor approximations to reformulate the MPC optimization problem as a convex second-order cone program that determines the PV panel position adjustments away from the sun-tracking trajectory. Through case studies, we demonstrate our approach, exploring the Pareto front between i) an approach that maximizes power production without considering crop needs and ii) crop yield with no agrivoltaics. We also conduct a case study exploring the impact of forecast error on MPC performance. We find that dynamically adjusting agrivoltaic panel position helps us actively manage the trade-offs between power production and crop yield, and that active panel control enables the agrivoltaic system to achieve land equivalent ratio values of up to 1.897.

title: Bifacial photovoltaic-micro agriculture integrated system for urban distributed energy applications: Optical-thermal coupling, realizable rear-side gains, and parallel carbon offsets
Hydrothermal conversion of lignocellulosic biomass using deep eutectic solvents and iron salts for solid biofuel and chemical recovery
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) of lignocellulosic waste (hemp oil cake) was investigated using a thermally stable choline chloride–glycolic acid deep eutectic solvent (DES) as an alternative reaction medium, in combination with iron salts (FeCl 3 and FeSO 4 ), to assess their synergistic effects on product properties. DES significantly enhanced biomass hydrolysis and solubilisation, while Fe salts modified reaction pathways and nutrient distribution. Compared to water-assisted HTC, DES-assisted HTC resulted in reduced hydrochar yields (50–72 wt%), particularly at higher temperatures and DES dosages, but promoted carbon enrichment. Carbon content increased from 49.6 wt% for water-derived hydrochar to 53.1–59.7 wt% for DES–Fe derived hydrochars, accompanied by a substantial reduction in nitrogen content. The combined DES–Fe HTC resulted in a notable improvement in fuel quality, with heating values reaching up to 26.6 MJ/kg. SEM showed increased porosity and spherical carbon structures. XPS and NMR confirmed enhanced aromatisation and nitrogen stabilisation in heterocyclic and graphitic forms, with Fe salts accelerating graphitic-N formation. DES-assisted HTC enriched process liquids in organic carbon, phenolics and furfural, indicating enhanced extraction but also increased ecotoxicity. No genotoxicity was detected in the Vicia faba assay. This work introduces a novel DES–Fe-assisted HTC approach to tailor hydrochar properties for renewable energy applications.

title: Bitcoin mining and renewable energy: Navigating sustainability, profitability, and electricity market dynamics
A multi-stage leaf-shaped solar distiller inspired by plant guttation for near-zero liquid discharge
Continuous direct solar-driven thermochemical energy storage via funnel-shape falling-particle reactors
Nanoparticles–functionalized kaolinite-based composite materials for multimodal energy conversion
Defrosting control strategy optimization of superhydrophobic air source heat pump aimed at minimizing defrosting duration and energy consumption
abstract: Superhydrophobic coatings have demonstrated excellent defrosting performance. However, its defrosting performance when used in air source heat pumps (ASHPs) is still unclear. To promote its application in ASHPs, two ASHPs with same configuration were manufactured, one superhydrophobic and the other hydrophilic. Through the microscopic observation and experimental analysis, its defrosting performance under the different frosting conditions were revealed. Then, the effects of compressor speed and defrosting termination conditions on defrosting performance were quantitatively analyzed, respectively. Finally, according the analysis results, a new defrosting control strategy suitable for superhydrophobic ASHPs was proposed and validated. Experimental results showed that the superhydrophobic ASHP exhibited excellent defrosting performance under different frosting conditions. Compared to those of hydrophilic ASHP, its defrosting durations at 2/1 °C and −3/-4 °C were 75 s and 165 s shorter, and the defrosting energy consumption was reduced by 62.8% and 64.5%. However, as the defrosting control strategy of hydrophilic ASHP was used, the superhydrophobic ASHP encountered the excessive defrosting issue. When adopting the proposed defrosting control strategy, i.e. the compressor speed was 46 rps and defrosting terminated when the surface temperature reached 2 °C and lasted 30 s, the goal of minimizing the defrosting duration and energy consumption was realized.

title: Inhibiting the formation of slag derived from K–Ca carbonate melts in gasifiers by tuning the ash fusion characteristics of woody biomass fuels through blending
Financing renewable energy projects in Latin America beyond resource quality, levelized cost of electricity, project feasibility, and the role of the weighted average cost of capital

Enhancing solar energy conversion via a coupled colloidal photovoltaic with thermally regenerative electrochemical conversion system
abstract: Efficient use of solar energy is limited by unavoidable heat losses during electricity generation, which reduces overall system performance. To address this challenge, this study introduces a hybrid solar energy system that combines a colloidal photovoltaic (CPV) with a thermally driven electrochemical unit capable of both power generation and cooling. A comprehensive numerical model is developed to describe the coupled electrical, thermal, and electrochemical interactions within the hybrid system, accounting for key irreversible losses. The effects of operating temperature, absorber thickness, regeneration efficiency, material properties, and internal resistance on system performance are systematically analyzed. Under optimal operating conditions, the hybrid system delivers a power density of 209.86 W m-2 and an energy efficiency of 20.99%, corresponding to improvements of 24.2% and 24.3%, respectively, relative to standalone CPV. The analysis further reveals that appropriate thermal management and parameter matching between subsystems are essential for fully unlocking the performance potential of the system. These findings demonstrate the viability of integrated solar-electrochemical systems to enhance solar energy utilization while simultaneously providing cooling, offering a promising pathway for advanced solar energy applications.

title: Techno-economic assessment of salt hydrate-based solar water heating systems under different climate scenarios
abstract: Large energy storage capacity and low cost of salt hydrates make them ideal candidates for integration into solar water heating systems. In this work, the phase-change performance and system reliability of the sodium acetate trihydrate–acetamide-based system and the sodium acetate trihydrate-based system were experimentally compared. The former system achieved a 5.6% higher efficiency. The system performance was further investigated numerically under varying setpoints and climate conditions to determine the optimal operating conditions for each material. Due to its more efficient use of latent heat, the sodium acetate trihydrate–acetamide-based system achieves a reduction of approximately 3.0% in annual cost compared to the sodium acetate trihydrate-based system at a setpoint of 40 °C in Hong Kong. However, the former system shows a longer payback period of approximately 4.9% in Denmark, and both phase-change materials showed negative net present values in France. The sodium acetate trihydrate–acetamide-based system exhibited lower energy use and operating expenditure under solar radiation of around 350–700 W/m 2 in Hong Kong. Nevertheless, after accounting for degradation, the higher replacement cost offset its operational savings, leading to a slightly higher lifecycle cost than the sodium acetate trihydrate-based system. This study highlights the importance of climate-specific material selection to balance energy performance and cost-effectiveness.

title: A novel combination of water-washing pre-treatment, varying briquetting techniques, and oxidative microwave torrefaction for the production of low-ash empty fruit bunch-based briquette with improved performance

Synthesis mechanism and combustion behavior of hybrid bio-coal synfuels from biomass and coal via synergistic co-carbonization technology
Multimodal wave energy conversion: Modal coupling effects and power capture
abstract: Multimodal wave energy converters offer theoretical performance advantages over single-mode devices, yet optimal design is hindered by limited understanding of modal interactions. This research study investigated modal coupling and veering phenomena across six configurations. The configurations employed pendulum geometries with symmetrically inclined power take-off tether systems. Their geometries, mass distributions, and draft were optimized to achieve target natural periods in heave, pitch, and surge. Modal analysis across various tether angles and power take-off stiffness revealed modal interaction and veering effects associated with surge-pitch coupling. These effects were linked to annual energy production metrics to identify optimal configurations for beneficial modal coupling. Results indicated that optimized multimodal wave energy converters can achieve superior energy production compared to equivalent single-mode heave absorbers. Combining modal analysis and power capture results, this paper demonstrates that characterizing coupling effects is a critical step in the system’s design.

title: An improved wake steering optimization method for enhanced wind energy production using realistic yaw behaviour
Operative performance of helical borehole heat exchanger with shape-stabilized phase change material: borehole array analysis
Long-term field performance of twin thin-film PV systems: A 14-year comparative study across two Spanish climatic zones
abstract: ABSTRACT Using 14 years of operational data, this study compares four small grid-connected thin-film photovoltaic systems installed as twin setups in Madrid and Jaén, Spain: a-Si (0.90 kW) and a-Si/μc-Si (0.88 kW). This configuration enables a controlled comparison between a more continental climate and warmer southern Mediterranean conditions. The a-Si systems were the best performers in terms of energy production, with average annual final system yields of 1537 kWh·kW -1 in Jaén and 1438 kWh·kW -1 in Madrid, and average annual performance ratios of 0.73 and 0.71, respectively. For a-Si/μc-Si, the corresponding values were lower: 1449 and 1361 kWh·kW -1 , and 0.68 and 0.67, respectively. Jaén generally outperformed Madrid, especially in winter, due to higher irradiance levels and slightly more favourable spectral conditions. However, a-Si/μc-Si showed slightly greater long-term stability. When regular cleaning was applied only in Jaén during a subperiod, the Madrid systems exhibited a more pronounced performance decline, revealing the role of soiling-related losses. Over the full analysis period, representative performance loss rates remained moderate, ranging from about −0.75 to −0.96 %·y -1 . Overall, this study provides a rare long-term field benchmark for legacy thin-film technologies, supporting PV lifetime modelling, performance-decline assessment, and the evaluation of emerging thin-film concepts under real operating conditions.

title: Improvement of the combustion model for a biomass stove: Validation with experimental measurements
abstract: In this work, two enhanced combustion models are used to study the overall performance of the Portable Patsari (PP) biomass stove. The 6R and 10R chemical mechanisms feature six and ten reactions, respectively, along with two values of the excess air ratio ( λ = 2 and 3). The main goal is to validate both models using experimental measurements by comparing key variables. The ANSYS Fluent software was used to build the following numerical configuration to simulate transport phenomena in the stove. The results showed that a better and more accurate assessment for the thermal and combustion performance was achieved by implementing 10R model than the 6R one. In general, there is good agreement between experimental measurements and simulations with λ = 3 . Also no significant differences in global efficiency and in most mass flow rates (MFR) were reported. The average contribution of the stove for 6R_L2 and 10R_L2 was found to be 0.63 ± 0.04 kgCO 2 e/kg (5%, p = 0.41) and 0.54 ± 0.05 kgCO 2 e/kg (11%, p = 0.11), respectively. This means that both models correctly predicted CO 2 e emissions. Finally, the insights constitute a substantial advance in the understanding of the combustion process in biomass plancha-type stoves. Given that the one-reaction combustion model is still in use, the results provide a more comprehensive study based on two upgraded combustion models.

title: 3D urban solar potential assessment using data-efficient deep learning in Lhasa (City of sunshine)
abstract: Low-carbon energy transitions are essential for climate change mitigation, yet urban solar potential assessments often emphasize rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems. Consequently, façade solar potential, solar-thermal (ST) yield, and solar supply–demand contributions are underexplored. It is an acute gap for Lhasa, China (“City of Sunshine”), where solar resources are abundant, but potential remains unquantified. The study proposes a three-dimensional assessment method integrating geographical potential (rooftop and façade solar radiation), technical potential (PV and ST outputs), and comprehensive potential (solar contribution to building energy consumption) to address this gap. A deep learning model for building height estimation was developed, reducing training images by 72.1% while cutting errors by 18.2%. A 3D urban model was derived, and three-tiered solar potential was calculated. The results highlight notable facades and ST potential. During the heating season, roofs and south facades receive comparable solar radiation. With an optimal PV-ST configuration, annual electricity production covers Lhasa’s residential demand, and thermal energy meets 69.5% of heating requirements. Solar energy supply proportion varies significantly across land use types and block forms. Transportation Land exhibits the highest solar energy supply proportion (54.5%), while Industrial and Mining Land shows the lowest (29.6%). High floor area ratio blocks can effectively utilize facade solar energy. The work extends solar potential analysis to include facades and thermal systems, providing an evaluation method adaptable to cities globally.

title: Machine learning model of hydrokinetic energy harnessing for tandem cylinders in flow-induced oscillation based on limited systemic data
Improving the overload performance of a Francis turbine by means of a passive vortex control device
abstract: The increasing demand for flexible operation of hydropower plants forces Francis turbines to operate frequently under off-design conditions, where draft-tube flow instabilities can severely limit performance and structural integrity. In particular, overload operation is associated with strong residual swirl at the runner outlet, leading to vortex-induced pressure pulsations and reduced pressure recovery. Despite its growing relevance, effective mitigation strategies specifically targeting overload conditions remain limited. This study proposes a novel passive vortex-control concept based on a bladed runner cone, inspired by boss-cap fins commonly used in marine propellers. The device is conceived as a minimally invasive retrofit solution aimed at reducing the tangential velocity component at the draft-tube inlet during high-discharge operation. Unsteady numerical simulations are performed on a medium–specific-speed Francis turbine over its entire operating range, from deep part load to overload conditions. The results show that the proposed device effectively suppresses overload vortex structures and significantly reduces draft-tube pressure pulsations, while improving diffuser pressure recovery. At the highest investigated discharge, an increase in hydraulic efficiency of up to approximately two percentage points is achieved, with only minor efficiency penalties at nominal and part-load conditions.

title: Data-driven temporal recursive thermal response model for borehole heat exchangers based on sum of exponential approximation
In situ test of vertical ground source heat pump system for space heating in Tunisia: energetic, economic and environment assessment
Comparing the sizing and costs of wind versus solar energy generation for a compressed hydrogen energy storage remote microgrid
abstract: Understanding the effects of renewable resource variation is critical to designing reliable and cost effective microgrid systems. Wind turbines and solar panels provide variable and intermittent generation of renewable energy due to the variable nature of the wind speed and solar irradiation. When combined with an energy storage approach such as hydrogen, a wind-hydrogen or solar-hydrogen microgrid system can be designed to reliably meet the energy demand of a remote installation. This study combines low‑order models of microgrid components to evaluate how different levels of renewable energy capacity relative to peak load affect system sizing and total cost. Representative wind speed and solar irradiance profiles over a one-week period are used along with load demand data from a naval base facility off the coast of southern California. Both the wind-hydrogen and solar-hydrogen configurations require the overbuilding of wind and solar power capacity relative to peak demand to achieve sustainability. The results indicate that for this location, the wind-hydrogen configuration can provide a cheaper sustainable solution compared to the solar-hydrogen configuration and to the current diesel-based energy infrastructure. Based on existing system economics and assumptions the model predicts the lowest upfront and long-term cost for a wind-hydrogen microgrid system is $8.94 million and 181.17 $/MWh respectively, compared to $10.94 million and 208.99 $/MWh for a solar-hydrogen microgrid system. This work provides important insight into the design and costs of wind and solar-based microgrids that can be applied at other locations.

A smart energy systems planning framework for high-renewable transitions in emerging energy systems: Application to Ghana
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of planning high-renewable energy transitions in rapidly developing energy systems facing increasing energy demand, fossil-fuel dependence, structural constraints, and limited flexibility. To this end, it develops and applies an integrated planning framework grounded in the Smart Energy Systems concept to evaluate pathways towards high shares of renewable energy under realistic system constraints. Ghana is used as a representative case study to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed framework in a Sub-Saharan African context. The analysis combines the characterisation of the national energy system, assessment of renewable resource potential, analysis of socio-economic drivers, and construction of a validated reference model. Four baseline high-renewable scenarios and two cost-optimised scenarios were evaluated using cost minimisation subject to ε-constraint bounds on electricity imports and exports. This enabled the identification of feasible combinations of photovoltaic, wind, and hydropower generation, complemented by battery and flywheel storage, while maintaining realistic electricity exchange balances. The results show that the selected transition pathway can reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately a factor of three, decrease fuel consumption from 131.7 TWh to 75 TWh annually, increase the renewable share of electricity to 95%, and expand renewable generation from 7.7 TWh to 40.2 TWh per year. The findings provide practical insights for renewable integration, storage planning, regional electricity trade-offs, and low-carbon transition strategies in Sub-Saharan Africa and comparable contexts.

Liquid air energy storage with high-grade molten salt heat recovery for enhanced round trip efficiency
High−performance silica nanosheet/carbon black supported platinum catalyst in high−temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells

Development of a system-efficiency-oriented offshore wind-hydrogen regulation framework for urban grid reliability
abstract: This paper develops an integrated wind-hydrogen regulation framework to effectively regulate urban power grid load using offshore wind energy, thereby improving grid reliability. To mitigate fluctuations in offshore wind power, this framework proposes a dual-path system model with hydrogen energy storage to enhance the system's wind power absorption capacity and regulation flexibility. Simultaneously, the framework also includes system capacity configuration optimization, aiming to find the optimal configuration using multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming (MOMILP) to maximize system efficiency. The framework is validated using real-world data from Hong Kong (2022). Results reveal distinct operational characteristics: under full-time regulation, the system achieves 95.4% system efficiency with minimal wind curtailment (0.7%); conversely, in peak-shaving mode, it prioritizes load satisfaction (32 GWh) but requires significantly higher capacity (197 GW) and results in lower efficiency (45.5%). Sensitivity analysis further highlights the dominance of conversion efficiency in peak-shaving scenarios. This work provides a critical technical reference for integrating offshore wind energy into the energy system and combining it with pure hydrogen energy storage to regulate urban power grid load and improve the overall reliability of the system.

Analysis of a building-integrated solar-driven multi-effect distillation system for Canadian Indigenous community applications
abstract: Many of Canada’s Indigenous populations depend on bottled water due to long-term drinking water advisories in their communities. Solar-powered multi-effect distillation has been demonstrated to be a sustainable solution for producing clean water for domestic use. However, there is a lack of research regarding its suitability for small-scale plants in northern climates. In this study, a building-integrated solar multi-effect distillation system is designed to meet the freshwater demand of a multi-unit residential building in a remote Indigenous community in Canada. Annual simulations carried out in TRNSYS assess the technical and economic performance using two types of solar thermal collectors: flat plate and evacuated tube. Simulations show that using a solar multi-effect distillation system with evacuated tube collectors can meet or exceed the water demand of a multi-unit residential building located in communities at or below a latitude of 59 degrees north in a cost-effective manner relative to current drinking water delivery options.

title: Wind-solar complementary hydrogen production strategy based on coordinated ratio and rotation optimization of heterogeneous electrolyzers

Governance and financing frameworks for hydrogen refueling stations under uncertainty: A hybrid MCDM analysis of the Northern Adriatic Hydrogen Valley
abstract: The decarbonization of road transport has positioned green hydrogen as a critical vector for sustainable mobility, particularly in hard-to-abate segments. Yet, the large-scale deployment of hydrogen refuelling stations (HRS) remains constrained by capital intensity, regulatory uncertainty, and demand volatility. Due to paucity of empirical evidence linking governance and financing models to HRS deployment pathways; this study develops a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making framework, combining Grey Relational Analysis and fuzzy-VIKOR, to prioritise ten operational, techno-economic and regulatory criteria and to determine the compartive ranking of five governance and financing models: Build–Operate–Transfer (BOT), Transfer–Operate–Transfer (TOT), Public-Private Partnership (PPP), Hydrogen-as-a-Service (HaaS) and Asset-Backed Securitisation (ABS). Given the early stage uncertanities the regulatory challenges, project risk, and demand uncertainty emerged as most prominent determinants with highest priority weights. HaaS and ABS appear effective as complementary mechanisms for smoothing capital requirements and diversifying investors when embedded in hybrid structures. Overall, the analysis underscores three key insights: (i) HRS deployment is constrained more by institutional design than by technological readiness; (ii) market-centric governance-framework and regulatory harmonization are essential for scalability; and (iii) PPP-based hybrid models offer a viable pathway to bolster the sustainable expansion of HRS infrastructure, particularly within transnational hydrogen valley initiatives.

title: Renewable hydrocarbon production via PPh3/NaI photoredox catalysis from derivatized fatty acid
abstract: Transitioning from fossil dependence toward sustainable fuel architecture requires green chemical pathways capable of generating drop-in hydrocarbon biofuels directly from biomass. Herein, we present a metal-free, visible-light-driven photoredox strategy employing a sodium iodide and triphenylphosphine (NaI/PPh 3 ) catalytic system for the selective hydrodecarboxylation of long-chain fatty acid-derived redox-active esters. Operating at room temperature (25 °C) and atmospheric pressure (1 atm) under blue LED irradiation (λ≈ 450 nm), and utilizing Hantzsch ester as a hydrogen donor, this protocol cleanly converts saturated fatty acid derivatives into linear n-alkanes C 9 –C 17 with yields up to 88%. The process eliminates the need for molecular hydrogen, noble-metal complexes, organic dye sensitizers, or high-temperature processing. The methodology was further adapted into a streamlined one-pot protocol directly from free fatty acids and successfully validated on mixed fatty acid feeds, yielding hydrocarbon distributions matched to sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and green diesel specifications. Mechanistic insights confirm the key role of an electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex in driving radical cleavage. Overall, this work establishes a benign, highly selective, and low-cost photochemical platform for converting renewable lipid derivatives into drop-in fuels.

Rainfall effects on biogas production at wastewater treatment plants
abstract: In this study, we quantify rainfall effects on biogas production using regression models and long-term daily operational data from wastewater treatment plants. Of particular attention is what we denote “first flush”, where rain following dry days brings sludge deposited in pipes, allowing the examination on how this process affects sludge deposition and biogas quality. From a case study in Denmark, we find first flush events are typically triggered when there has been no significant rainfall for three to four consecutive days followed by a daily rainfall exceeding 2 mm. A significant negative effect of rainfall was only found in secondary sludge separation but not in primary sludge separation. Although rainfall directly dilutes wastewater, the first flush event can increase the deposition of sludge thereby also increase the methane in biogas. On-site, the resulting increase in biogas-based electricity generation partially offsets the additional energy demand caused by rainfall, highlighting a self-balancing mechanism of rainfall effects. Rolling average regressions showed that rainfall in general (i.e. not first flush) directly and significantly reduced biogas production within 9 - 12 days by 1.94%–5.50%, and the electricity consumption response to rainfall was more evident on the following day.

Response-based scaling and design optimization of small-scale floating offshore wind turbine prototypes
abstract: Laboratory testing supports the modeling and design optimization of floating offshore wind turbines, yet full-scale testing is often impractical due to cost, safety, and limited flexibility for design iteration. Model-scale testing provides an alternative. However, conventional model-scale approaches face fundamental similarity limitations, as Froude and Reynolds similitude cannot be simultaneously satisfied at small scales due to wind tunnel velocity, blockage, and operational constraints. This study presents a numerical response-based dynamic similarity framework. It preserves selected system-level responses rather than enforcing strict classical similitude. Three metrics are used: (1) the ratio between excitation (i.e., from aerodynamic rotor loads and hydrodynamic forcing) and primary natural frequencies, (2) the damping ratio for the pitch motion, and (3) normalized platform pitch rotation and tower-tip bending deflection. A reduced-order coupled model, combining a linear six-degree-of-freedom platform representation, an Euler–Bernoulli tower model, and a Blade Element Momentum rotor formulation is developed. The NREL 5-MW turbine on the OC4-DeepCwind semi-submersible is used as a reference case for benchmarking. The framework is benchmarked against full-scale OpenFAST simulations. A constrained optimization determines rotor geometry, tower properties, and ballast distribution. Results show that the proposed approach reproduces the selected similarity metrics with deviations of approximately 4 − 12 % in frequency ratio, damping characteristics, pitch response, and structural deformation. The methodology provides a low-cost and manufacturable design pathway for response-matched model-scale prototypes. Physical testing of the optimized design is outside the scope of the present study and is reserved for future work.
