Anaerobic co-digestion of lignocellulose and ammonia rich biomasses using advanced composite bioaugmentation inocula
abstract: Lignocellulose- and ammonia-rich biomasses are widely available and offer substantial potential for methane generation, yet their combined use often severely inhibits anaerobic digestion (AD) performance. This study explored bioaugmentation as a strategy to counteract the simultaneous inhibitory effects of lignocellulose and ammonia. Composite microbial inocula, consisting of hydrolytic bacteria and methanogenic archaea, were developed from mixed cultures and pure strains (i.e., Ruminococcus albus and Methanoculleus bourgensis ). These cultures were acclimated to elevated lignocellulose (3 g VS L -1 ) and ammonia (4 g NH 4 + -N L -1 ) concentrations. To assess long-term preservation methods suitable for practical future commercial use, the acclimatised inocula were either lyophilised or immobilised in gel. Their performance was then assessed in batch reactors operating under high lignocellulose and/or ammonia levels. The lyophilised composite inoculum containing acclimatised M. bourgensis and R. albus achieved the highest methane yield, reaching 195 ml CH 4 g -1 VS, which was sixfold higher than its gel-immobilised counterpart. In addition, the lyophilised composite inoculum derived from acclimatised mixed inoculum exhibited a rapid initial methane production response and produced 235.1% more methane than its corresponding abiotic control. This study demonstrated, for the first time, the successful development of composite bioaugmentation inocula combining hydrolytic and methanogenic microorganisms that are acclimatised to harsh lignocellulose and ammonia levels, while also being suitable for extended storage and on-demand use, offering promising potential for improving AD process stability and efficiency.

title: System interactions constraining offshore wind deployment in the Dutch North Sea
abstract: The Netherlands aims to deploy up to 70 GW of offshore wind by 2050 in its waters. As one of the busiest sea areas in the world, the Dutch part of the North Sea is shaped by spatial tensions and a degraded state of nature due to activities such as fossil fuel extraction, shipping and fishing. The interconnectedness of sectors and actors leads to various interactions with spatially demanding offshore wind, potentially enabling and constraining its deployment. We use systems thinking to explore the interactions which occur in the Dutch North Sea as a result of the offshore wind transition. We interview 22 stakeholders, organise one structured focus group discussion, and four follow-up workshops. Through our systems thinking approach, we elucidate on the interactions between different sectors and activities in the domains of the socio-technical system of offshore wind, spatial competition, and quality of nature, thereby broadening the scope of analysis. This allows us to identify a set of interactions which impact the deployment of offshore wind in the Netherlands, located in the domains infrastructure, society, space, and ecology. Overall, we find that the spatial and ecological interactions point to the need to build on synergies between different activities for a successful transition. As the expansion of offshore wind will lead to a variety of effects due to the interactions with other domains, there will likely be conflicts with other policy areas such as ecology and marine spatial planning.

title: Optimizing specific dark fermentation strategies for enhanced bio-hydrogen production from different agricultural wastes
abstract: The integration of the dark fermentation process into existing anaerobic digestion plants, leading to the implementation of two stage processes, may enable the sequential recovery of biohydrogen and biomethane from agricultural residues. This study evaluated semi-continuous dark fermentation of cattle manure, corn residue, and soybean residue at hydraulic retention times of 3–10 days, including co-fermentation and digestate recirculation strategies. Cattle manure did not support stable biohydrogen production under the tested conditions, producing no detectable hydrogen and rapidly shifting towards methanogenesis. CR showed only transient biohydrogen peaks, followed by process instability associated with pH decrease, nutrient limitation, and methanogenic competition. Soybean residue supported stable hydrogen production at HRT 3 d, reaching 4.7 NmLH 2 /gVS. The best performance was obtained by soybean/CR co-fermentation, which achieved 12.4 NmLH 2 /gVS, 67.8 NmLgas/gVS, and 0.32 gCODVFA/gVS. VFA production was strongly substrate-dependent, with CR at HRT 7 d reaching the highest VFA yield among single-substrate trials. Biomethane potential tests showed that fermented effluents retained relevant residual energy potential, with fermented CR increasing biomethane recovery by up to 34% compared with the untreated substrate. Overall, the results demonstrate that substrate selection and nutrients balance are key factors for implementing two-stage anaerobic digestion of agricultural residues.

title: Process simulation of green ammonia production plant and waste heat recovery system for integration into Finnish district heating networks and energy infrastructure
abstract: An integrated process simulation model is developed to study the utilization of waste heat recovered from an industrial scale green ammonia production plant in Finland. ASPEN Plus was used to simulate the steady-state production of green hydrogen via alkaline electrolysis and it´s subsequent synthesis into ammonia through the Haber Bosch process. The plant behaviour is simulated under varying power levels, hydrogen mass flow rates and district heating supply temperatures using a MATLAB code to estimate the annual hourly recoverable waste heat for two district heating networks i.e. Kokkola and Oulu in Finland. The simulations targeted an annual ammonia production of approximately 213kt and evaluated waste heat recovery potential and district heating integration feasibility. The study reveals that the plant can generate up to 115 MW of usable waste heat, confirming its potential as a significant thermal energy source. Dynamic simulations showed seasonal variation in waste heat availability. In Oulu, a 47.16 MW district heat (DH) production system caused only 0.2% DH curtailment, while in Kokkola a 23.58 MW system resulted in 12% curtailment, highlighting the importance of site-specific, moderately sized heat pump integration for stable operation. Results indicate that although waste heat is continuously generated, its high volume relative to demand particularly during summer is limited due to feasibility constraints.

title: Assessment of fuel property enhancement toward TRL advancement in biomass torrefaction

Multi-criteria decision-making for net zero transition in energy islands: A case study in South Italy
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving net-zero emissions in islanded and remote areas presents unique challenges due to energy supply limitations, high reliance on fossil fuels, and environmental constraints. This study applies Multi-Criteria Decision-Making methods to support energy planning for the transition to net zero on Favignana Island, Italy. Using real consumption data from the local community, it evaluates renewable energy deployment strategies, considering technical feasibility and socio-environmental implications. The novelty of the study lies in coupling HOMER Pro scenario optimization with Fuzzy AHP-TOPSIS to rank island transition pathways across technical, economic, environmental, and social criteria. LCOE, reliability, and social acceptance emerged as the most influential criteria according to pairwise comparisons developed by 3 experts, with weights of 0.2552, 0.2294, and 0.1864, respectively. Under the adopted assumptions, the grid-connection scenario ranked highest, achieving a TOPSIS relative closeness index of 0.7884, compared to 0.3104 of Rooftop PV, 0.1893 of Utility scale PV, and 0.2704 of Hybrid PV and Wind solutions. A sensitivity analysis confirmed the robustness of the ranking, showing that the grid-connection scenario remains the preferred option under a wide range of variations in criteria weights and key input assumptions. The study offers a replicable framework for energy decision-making in other insular or off-grid contexts.

title: Technical evaluation of bio-Fischer-Tropsch wax co-processing in industrial hydrocracking: a scalable pathway to lower-carbon fuels
abstract: The integration of renewable feedstocks into conventional refinery operations is a key pathway for accelerating decarbonization in the fuels sector. Among the available options, bio-based Fischer–Tropsch (FT) wax provides a chemically compatible and scalable route for refinery co-processing. In practice, such integration is most effectively implemented in hydrocracking units, which are highly sensitive to feedstock properties. A clear understanding of how renewable FT wax affects unit performance and product quality is therefore essential for reliable deployment. This study presents a rigorous evaluation of bio-FT wax co-processing in an industrial-scale hydrocracking unit using advanced simulations validated against operational plant data, ensuring high fidelity and practical relevance. A comprehensive set of blending scenarios was examined to quantify the influence of bio-FT wax on feed impurity mitigation, reactor thermodynamics, hydrogen consumption, and product distribution over the future implementation roadmap. The results reveal that increasing bio-FT wax content substantially reduces feed contaminants, lowers hydrogen demand, and moderates exothermic reactor profiles, while maintaining product yields and properties within specification limits. These findings demonstrate the technical viability and operational robustness of integrating bio-derived FT wax into existing hydrocracking infrastructure, highlighting its potential as a scalable, near-term pathway to produce lower-carbon fuels suitable for high-demand sectors such as aviation.

Economic potential of the energy transition: A regionalized input-output analysis of wind power in Lower Saxony, Germany
abstract: Wind power is crucial for the energy transition, but regional impacts are still underexplored. This study analyzes the impact of regional datasets for examining the economic footprint and multipliers of regional wind power, differentiating between technology type and lifetime phase. Additionally, the economic and environmental impacts of wind power expansion are evaluated. Lower Saxony, a pioneering wind power region in Northern Germany, is used as a case study. The methodological approach involves constructing a regional input-output table, integrating wind power sectors and developing scenarios consistent with policy objectives. Results reveal the significant economic footprint of wind power in Lower Saxony and emphasize the importance of detailed regional datasets. Onshore wind key component manufacturing and offshore wind installation generate the highest economic multipliers. Offshore wind has greater economic impacts per unit of electricity than onshore wind. Wind power expansion can create substantial gross economic gains, but outcomes strongly depend on regional supply chain integration. Net effects include job losses and substantial reductions in emissions and water use. Policy implications include strengthening upstream industries, coping with labor market dynamics, and enhancing regionalized data collection. The study highlights the need for spatially focused approaches to capture the regional dimension of the energy transition.

title: Critical roles of anion identity in activating potassium-modified Fe-based oxygen carriers in biomass chemical looping gasification
Solar-driven tubular Co2(OH)PO4/carbon nitride S-scheme heterojunctions for renewable H2 production and CO2 reduction to solar fuels
Ruthenium nanoparticles embedded in Mn-doped Fe5Ni4S8 pentlandite with outstanding bifunctional electrolytic hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions
Accurate installation angle determination for bifacial photovoltaics using hybrid parameter extraction and outdoor experiments
abstract: Bifacial photovoltaic modules achieve higher energy yield than monofacial systems by capturing irradiance on both surfaces, but accurately predicting performance remains challenging due to complex optical–thermal–electrical interactions. This study develops and experimentally validates a coupled optical–thermal–electrical model for bifacial photovoltaic modules under real outdoor conditions in Tehran, Iran. The framework integrates view-factor geometry for optical analysis, multi-layer heat transfer modeling, and a single-diode electrical formulation. A hybrid optimization procedure combining a genetic algorithm extracts electrical parameters, ensuring robust convergence and accurate identification. The model is validated against experimental measurements from a 580 W bifacial module, achieving a mean absolute percentage error of 4.61% for predicted power. Parametric analyses investigate the effects of tilt angle and azimuth orientation. Results show that at a tilt angle equal to site latitude (35°), annual energy yields of east–west and south-facing configurations are nearly identical (1286.3 vs. 1279.5 kWh)—a finding contrary to conventional monofacial behavior. The validated model provides a reliable tool for predicting bifacial photovoltaic performance, optimizing installation geometry, and supporting system design. This assessment framework offers practical guidance for maximizing energy yield in semi-arid regions and similar environments.

title: Quantification of building demand uncertainty on the operational performance evaluation and capacity optimizations in building microgrid system design
An exergoeconomic exploration of a solar-driven humidification-dehumidification desalination
Advanced wind-cooling coordination by tensor train based higher order dynamic mode decomposition
abstract: The global transition to a carbon-neutral energy system faces a significant challenge due to the rapid increase in building cooling requirements. Integrating wind energy, which is cost-competitive but highly intermittent, into building cooling processes presents a promising way to achieve sustainable development. However, because of the significant temporal and spatial mismatch between supply and demand, it still encounters challenges. To address this issue, a new framework is proposed that combines tensor train decomposition and higher order dynamic mode decomposition. This framework starts by compressing high-dimensional temporal and spatial dynamics into a low-rank tensor train format. Then, higher order dynamic mode decomposition is applied to identify the dominant temporal and spatial modes, and their dynamic behaviors. This enables the implementation of an effective model predictive control strategy for real-time coordination. Compared with existed methods such as canonical polyadic decomposition and long short-term memory networks, the proposed framework reduces the amount of wind curtailment by 7.2% and operating costs by 21.4%–25.2% while maintaining thermal comfort violation rates below 3.5%. Furthermore, the framework achieves 95.1% prediction accuracy with an online computation time of only 0.45 s per control step, fully meeting real-time requirements.

title: Effect of steam-enriched CO2 atmosphere on the properties of biochar derived from food waste gasification
abstract: Agro-industrial residues (food waste) represent a significant source of feedstocks that possess, both material and energy potentials. This study examined the valorisation of sunflower husks, buckwheat husks, cherry stones, and tomato waste through gasification under CO 2 and steam-enriched CO 2 atmospheres at 900 °C. The biochemical composition of these feedstocks was characterised by 28–78 wt% lignocellulosic fractions content and from 0.6 to 17 wt% of lipids. Solid residue (biochar) yields ranged from 9.1% (sunflower husks, CO 2 + H 2 O) to 28.1% (tomato waste, CO 2 ), while carbon content reached up to 88 wt% for cherry stone. The introduction of steam reduced the yield by 35%, but significantly increased the specific surface area from 410 to 881 m 2 /g and from 224 to 823 m 2 /g for buckwheat husks and sunflower husks, respectively. Lignin-rich feedstocks produced more aromatic and thermally stable structures (R 50 > 0.45). FT-IR spectra confirmed the loss of hydroxyl and carbonyl groups and formation of condensed aromatic structures. These findings show that biochemical composition of food waste significantly influences carbonisation behaviour and surface functionality. Furthermore, they provide a framework for optimizing gasification conditions to produce biochars that can be used as bio-based materials in catalysis, adsorption, and carbon sequestration.

title: Hydrothermally synthesized sites of NiFe-LDHs anchored on the biomass-derived hydrochar for electrocatalytic performance

Carnot battery integrated with ultra-high-temperature heat pump and parabolic trough collector for hybrid PV-concentrating solar power plants
Sustainable biogas upgrading using renewable ammonia from pig slurry: integration of microbial electrolysis cells and hydrophobic membrane technology
abstract: Biogas upgrading is required to increase methane concentration and meet grid-injection standards. Conventional absorbents such as monoethanolamine (MEA) and synthetic ammonium hydroxide (NH 4 OH) provide high CO 2 removal but involve high costs, energy-intensive regeneration, and non-renewable resources. This study proposes an integrated approach coupling ammonium recovery from pig slurry in microbial electrolysis cells (MEC) with its reuse as a CO 2 absorbent in hollow fiber membrane contactors (HFMC). The recovered ammonium was evaluated against water, MEA, and synthetic NH 4 OH under different gas-to-liquid ratios and absorbent concentrations. Water achieved limited CH 4 enrichment (∼80%), whereas MEA and synthetic NH 4 OH provided >90% CO 2 removal. MEC-derived ammonium achieved >95% CH 4 and <2% CO 2 with real biogas, demonstrating its potential as a renewable absorbent. This dual valorisation approach enhances the economic and environmental sustainability of biogas upgrading, positioning MEC-derived ammonium as a viable alternative to conventional absorbents.

title: Assessing the potential for floating offshore wind farms in Irish waters: A comprehensive methodology and findings
abstract: ABSTRACT The potential of Irish waters to support floating offshore wind farms has not been fully recognised. A novel and robust methodology has been developed and implemented to address this research question and define the capabilities of floating offshore wind energy in Irish waters. This approach features a meticulous selection of hierarchically organised criteria aligned with legislation, policy, and best practices from the wind industry. The delineated area identifies locations where floating offshore wind farms could possibly be developed with limited technical and legal risk. Additionally, the study outlines key characteristics of the area, including bathymetry, wind conditions, total installed capacity, and energy yield. The identified area for potential development comprises only 13.7% of the initially surveyed section of the exclusive economic zone; nonetheless, it has substantial potential, capable of hosting a total power capacity of 246 GW or 307 GW, depending on the layout scenario. Remarkably, nearly 80% of this power can be developed in water depths up to 200 m. Furthermore, the capacity factor of the reference wind turbine ranges from 56.7% to 64.1%, with a gross annual energy output of between 53.1 and 59.9 GWh per year per wind turbine.

Technical assessment of Agave sisalana leaves as feedstock for integrated first- and second-generation ethanol production
abstract: Agave sisalana , widely cultivated in northeastern Brazil, holds great socioeconomic importance, although its leaves remain underutilized. This study evaluated their potential as feedstock for integrated first- (1G) and second-generation (2G) ethanol production. In the 1G route, leaf juice underwent acid hydrolysis and fermentation, yielding 40.70 g/L ethanol with 74.00% efficiency using Ethanol Red®. In the 2G route, a fractional factorial design optimized bagasse pretreatment; the best condition (30 min, 180°C, 15% solids, 0.5% acid) achieved 60.31% cellulose and 80.32% hemicellulose conversion. Although inhibitors were generated, detoxification enabled efficient fermentation, resulting in 27.44 g/L ethanol with an 83.59% yield using the GMO strain Celere2L. Overall, 80.90 L of ethanol per ton of leaves was obtained, demonstrating A. sisalana 's potential as a sustainable feedstock for integrated 1G–2G ethanol production and reinforcing its relevance for biofuel development and energy diversification in semi-arid regions.

Increase in corn ethanol production in Brazil: Examining changes in dynamic interconnectedness
abstract: Brazil is a major producer of ethanol in the world. Traditionally, this type of production is derived from sugarcane. However, in recent years, the increase in corn production in the country has directed part of this surplus toward corn-based ethanol. This movement has changed biofuel production dynamics to new areas in the country’s Center-West, where grain production is dominant. Therefore, this study examines the dynamic connectedness between regional ethanol and corn prices in Brazil. A TVP-VAR model was applied, considering the specifications proposed by Antonakakis et al. (2020). First, we examined the transmission between the major sugarcane-based ethanol region in the southeast and the new corn-based ethanol region in the Center-West. Second, we examined the regional interconnectedness between ethanol and corn in the Center-West production spots. DCC-GARCH and wavelet coherence analysis were also applied to complement the regional analysis. The results indicate an increase in ethanol volatility connectedness between producing states after the corn-based ethanol outbreak in 2019/20. At the regional level, our findings suggest a slight increase in the connection between ethanol and corn prices, especially in the state of Mato Grosso, where significant co-movements were observed in the recent period. These findings are important to show that the new ethanol feedstock in Brazil can potentially affect ethanol price volatility dynamics at the country level as well as the contagion between corn and ethanol at the regional level.

title: Quantifying microbial, enzymatic, and acid-driven pathways of lignocellulose degradation and their impact on methane production in Sudangrass silage

Experimental and numerical characterization of a large-stroke winch-based power take-off for wave energy converters
abstract: Point absorber wave energy converters face critical survivability and efficiency challenges due to limited stroke constraints and destructive end-stop collisions in extreme seas. This study presents a 1 kW-scale winch-driven power take-off system with a 10 m active stroke, designed to geometrically decouple the internal drivetrain from constrained motion rails. To evaluate the drivetrain without hydrodynamic uncertainty, land-based crane trials imposed repeatable 10 m tether displacements, while the prescribed 1 m/s line velocity was selected to be broadly consistent with a 1:6 Froude-scaled representation of full-scale extreme vertical motion. The controlled actuation isolated the internal energy cascade and enabled stage-wise separation of speed-dependent mechanical losses from load-dependent electromagnetic losses across resistive loads of 4.5 to 45 Ω. Experiments identified an optimal internal conversion efficiency near 18 Ω, beyond which high-current effects degraded performance. Diagnostic analysis further showed that constant-parameter generator predictions failed when stator current exceeded the 5.16 A rated limit, causing over-predictions of current, torque, and electrical power due to armature reaction and magnetic saturation. To capture this behavior, a multi-domain physics-based model combined a no-load-calibrated viscous rotational damper with a current-dependent back electromotive force coefficient roll-off profile. This correction eliminated high-current prediction bias and restored agreement across the mechanical-to-electrical energy cascade. These findings demonstrate that single-point static tuning is insufficient under transient overloads. The validated model supports future upscaling and parameter-scheduled load control to maintain optimal operation, mitigate saturation, and maximize wave-to-wire energy extraction in irregular seas.

title: Sequencing batch high-rate algal ponds: An alternative approach to sustainable biodiesel and ALE production with microalgae-bacteria consortia cultivated in domestic wastewater
abstract: High-rate algal ponds (HRAP) are cost-effective systems for producing microalgal-bacterial aggregates from wastewater, forming a consortium rich in alginate-like exopolymers (ALE) and lipids suitable for third-generation biodiesel. However, the effects of sequencing batch (SB) operation in HRAP remain unknown. Therefore, the present study evaluated the dynamics of algal genera, sewage treatment, ALE and lipid contents, and biodiesel quality of an HRAP (2400 L) operated in SB over 134 days. After the consortium formation (d0-d20), the pond reached a stability period between days 66 and 128, demonstrating a relative abundance of >80% of Cyclotella sp. and nitrogen, phosphorus, and chemical oxygen demand removals of 90.1 ± 3.7%, 40.1 ± 7.3%, and 66.6% ± 7.6%, respectively. ALE content reached 87.4 ± 19.3 mg/gTSS. The most efficient extraction (Soxhlet + chloroform: methanol 2:1) yielded an average lipid content of 11 ± 2 %, and the most abundant methyl esters were C16:0 (35.74%), C18:0 (21.01%), and C16:1 (12.08%). The biodiesel produced met international standards for cetane number, iodine value, kinematic viscosity, and density, while also exhibiting a higher heating value consistent with other renewable energy sources, such as soybean. These results imply increased flexibility in the use of HRAP-MABA systems through SB operation and demonstrate the production of high-quality biodiesel from predictable biomass, even under the adverse conditions of open systems.

title: High-fidelity numerical simulation and performance analysis of Magnus-effect vertical axis wind turbine
Ultrasound-enhanced selective fermentation improves lipid recovery from microalgae
Pyrolysis and combustion of crude glycerol-based de-oiled yeast: analyses and kinetic modeling
abstract: Biomass is essential for the production of both energy and high-value products, making the diversification of sources necessary. De-oiled yeast is a waste obtained after oil extraction from oleaginous yeast. The study investigates the pyrolysis and combustion behaviors of de-oiled yeast biomass (G-DYB) under heating rates of 5, 10, and 15 °C.min -1 , the oleaginous yeast being cultivated with crude glycerol as carbon source. Kinetic modeling is performed applying the Extended Independent Parallel Reaction model with eight constituents, or other tools. The optimal values of the activation energy lie between 38 and 106 kJ.mol -1 for pyrolysis and between 35 and 155 kJ.mol -1 for combustion, which are relatively low compared to those obtained for conventional biomass. A deconvolution procedure specifies the contributions of the eight constituents which are identified considering the chemical composition of G-DYB. The calculated values of conventional indices indicate potential slagging and fouling issues. The study also analyzes the main gaseous emissions occurring during pyrolysis and combustion at 5 °C.min -1 . The results of the study will contribute to optimizing the thermal degradation of G-DYB at an industrial scale.

title: Oxidative torrefaction of brewers' spent grain: Fuel property enhancement and substantial energy efficiency improvement
abstract: Torrefaction has emerged as a promising pretreatment technology for enhancing the fuel properties of biomass. By introducing controlled oxidation reactions that supply in-situ exothermic heat, oxidative torrefaction significantly improves both fuel properties and overall energy efficiency. In this study, oxidative torrefaction of brewers' spent grain was performed, where the influences of torrefaction temperature (200-300°C), residence time (15-30 min), and oxygen concentration (0-21 vol.%) on torrefaction performance were systematically investigated. Results show that oxidative torrefaction yields superior fuel properties, doubling the Energy-Mass Co-benefit Index at 250°C for 30 min. FTIR and TG-MS analyses confirm intensified deoxygenation. Oxidative conditions accelerate torrefaction rate and extent, significantly reducing processing time and improving energy efficiency. When EMCI exceeds 10, electrical energy consumption is reduced by over 40%. TG-DSC analysis reveals that inert torrefaction at 250°C requires heat equivalent to 3.82% of the final product's calorific value, whereas oxidative torrefaction (13.5 vol% O2) supplies 37.66% of its own heat demand. Overall, high temperature (300°C), short duration (15 min), and moderate oxygen concentration (13.5 vol%) achieve the best comprehensive performance. This work provides systematic insights into fuel performance and energy efficiency of oxidative torrefaction, offering new directions for process optimization and industrial application.

Diagnosing subseasonal thermal memory and thermal interference from operational data in a dense urban GWHP network
abstract: Urban groundwater heat pump networks are expanding quickly, intensifying heat accumulation and raising concerns about long-term sustainability. We apply a data-driven diagnostic framework to 35 systems in Zaragoza’s alluvial aquifer (2016–2024), analysing 7.48 million measurements. By integrating polar-density plots, cross-correlations on deseasonalised residuals and seasonally integrated series, and residual coherence analyses, the framework quantifies injection-to-production response and thermal-plume redistribution timescales, evaluates how long injection- and production-temperature signals remain coupled, and classifies likely intra- and intersystem interference from routinely monitored data. Observed delays of 33–45 days in the production-temperature response to injection-temperature variations, together with 110–122-day timescales for redistribution of the thermal plume, indicate that the monitored network exhibits subseasonal thermal memory. Around 69% of systems show intra- or intersystem interference, while 31% display low-amplitude signals (<2 °C) consistent with urban heat-island background or distal attenuated plumes. Thermal impact at the production well increases at 0.12 °C yr -1 , three times the injection trend, evidencing cumulative warming and plume superposition under cooling-dominated network operation. Even with Darcy velocities of up to 3.24 m d -1 , rapid groundwater flow did not prevent subseasonal thermal effects from persisting at network scale. Coordinated operation, thermal-load balancing and recovery-oriented well design could reduce interference and cumulative warming. The methodology provides transferable diagnostics to characterise groundwater heat pump behaviour in urban aquifers and inform the planning and management of dense groundwater heat pump networks.

title: An efficient prediction strategy for biogas yields based on machine learning and private optimization technique

Carbon capture and oxy-combustion for glassmaking decarbonization through Power-to-Gas: technical and economic viability assessment
abstract: Decarbonization of the glass industry is addressed through indirect electrification achieved by the production and use of renewable synthetic methane under Power-to-Gas integration schemes. The CO 2 captured in the glass furnace reacts with e-hydrogen to produce renewable methane which substitutes the fossil natural gas currently burnt. Four novel low-carbon concepts are compared with a container conventional plant from techno-economic viewpoint. They mainly differ in the carbon capture technology: (1) calcium looping with replacement of raw material by CaO purge; (2) amine scrubbing, (3) oxy-glass melting with O 2 -CO 2 atmosphere, and (4) pure oxy-combustion in the melting furnace. Besides comparison of energy penalty and CO 2 emission reduction, the economic impact of implementing abatement technologies is analysed under three economic scenarios: full electricity purchase and self-production via photovoltaic or wind farm. In all cases, the natural gas consumption is reduced to 95%, but the maximum CO 2 reductions are achieved with pure oxy-combustion (96%). When combined with wind self-production, the amine case presents the best carbon abatement (60 €/t CO2 ) and specific implementation costs (13 €/t glass ) for a plant of 250 t glass /d. However, at bigger plant sizes (600 t glass /d) the pure oxy-combustion presents comparable results (51 €/t CO2 and 14 €/t glass ) to the amines case (57 €/t CO2 and 12 €/t glass ).

title: Experimental and numerical study of a shell-and-tube latent thermal energy storage for solar thermal applications
abstract: Shell-and-tube latent thermal energy storage plays a key role in buffering intermittent solar heat supply and ensuring reliable hot-water delivery in solar thermal systems. Previous studies have shown that shell-side flow maldistribution can cause short-circuiting and uneven heating between phase change material tubes, thereby degrading thermal performance. To address this issue, a perforated-plate-assisted latent thermal energy storage prototype was experimentally investigated, and a validated numerical model was used to clarify its internal thermodynamic behavior. The results show that the perforated plate markedly improves shell-side flow distribution and leads to excellent inter-tube uniformity during both charging and discharging. The liquid-fraction non-uniformity index between tubes is only 0.012 during charging and 0.0017 during discharging. However, the dominant non-uniformity appears as vertical stratification within individual tubes, with corresponding indices of 0.09 and 0.11. This vertical non-uniformity reduces effective heat utilization and degrades exergy performance. Higher flow rates enhance both charging and discharging rates. The maximum charging power and heat exchange capacity rate reach 3.1 kW and 343.61 W/K, respectively, while the maximum useful discharging power and heat exchange capacity rate reach 13.31 kW and 608.37 W/K. However, for practical domestic hot water applications, higher flow rates involve a trade-off: they increase hot water yield, but also lead to higher charging energy demand, lower average outlet temperature, and shorter useful supply duration. These findings show that the perforated plate effectively mitigates inter-tube non-uniformity, while future optimization should focus on suppressing intra-tube vertical stratification and adapting the flow-rate strategy to specific domestic hot water demands.

title: Performance analysis of solar desalination unit coupled with latent heat energy storage tank for stable freshwater production
Energy, exergy, economic and environmental (4E) analysis of a hybrid power plant fed by sugarcane residues
abstract: One of the main challenges for the sugarcane sector is to develop efficient and low-cost solutions for energy recovery from residues generated during sugar and ethanol production. In this context, this work proposes a novel integrated energy system that simultaneously processes typical sugarcane residues (bagasse, straw, vinasse, and filter cake). While recent literature has predominantly explored thermochemical or biochemical routes, the proposed architecture introduces a Rankine and Brayton combined cycle in a conventional mill, without affecting the sugar and ethanol production. A numerical model on the Excel/VBA platform is developed to simulate steady state operation conditions and calculate energy, exergy, economic, and environmental (4E) indicators. The hybrid configuration provides predictable power generation during the sugarcane season, reaching an electricity production of 74.1 kWh e per tonne of sugarcane milled (TC), a value significantly higher than that reported for conventional sugarcane plants (34.1 kWh e /TC). An exergy efficiency of 28.9% and a carbon footprint of 44.97 kg CO2eq /MWh e are achieved, alongside a competitive levelized cost of energy of 26.31 USD/MWh e . The approach can be implemented in a short timeframe for both new and existing facilities. Consequently, hybrid sugarcane plants may emerge as a reliable alternative that strategically complements intermittent renewable energy sources.

Understanding supported magnesium chloride sorbent materials for sorption-enhanced ammonia synthesis toward renewable hydrogen storage
abstract: As the world shifts to renewable energy, ammonia is emerging as a promising green alternative to hydrogen due to its high energy density and carbon neutrality. While conventional ammonia synthesis relies on energy-intensive condensation process to separate ammonia from unreacted gases following the catalytic reaction, metal halides offer a potential alternative for process intensification in renewable-driven ammonia production. However, moisture sensitivity hinders their applicability. Research on ammonia separation with metal halides often prioritizes absorption capacity, overlooking detailed sorbent characterization due to water contamination challenges. This study investigates MgCl 2 -impregnated porous supports, focusing on efficient characterization under inert conditions and ammonia sorption capacity. Porous supports improve material stability, reduce swelling, and enable long-term sorption by accommodating volume changes and enhancing kinetics. Results show that chemical absorption of ammonia by MgCl 2 is the predominant mechanism determining sorption capacity. Among tested materials, MgCl 2 /ZSM-5 achieves the highest sorption capacity (335 mg/g at 25 °C), while MgCl 2 /USY (500) excels in cyclic stability; however, capacity declines at higher temperatures. These findings emphasise the significance of considering support acidity and moisture effects in designing ammonia sorbents for renewable energy-integrated processes. Additionally, new mechanistic ammonia absorption/desorption kinetic model was developed, enabling future efficient CFD simulation for sorption-enhanced N 2 activation.

title: Optimization of sandstone geothermal reinjection: Integrating field tests, numerical simulations and machine learning
Decarbonization of a sugarcane refinery in Mexico through bioethanol production and CHP generation with carbon capture and storage (BECCS)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive strategy for the decarbonization of an existing sugarcane refinery through the integration of bioethanol production, combined heat and power (CHP) generation using bagasse, and Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS), collectively forming a Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS) system. This study defines a base scenario (BS) with a typical Mexican sugarcane mill, Ingenio Motzorongo, producing sugar, molasses, anhydro ethanol as oxygenate agent of gasoline and including combined heat and power (CHP) from sugarcane bagasse combustion. Also, we propose an alternative scenario (AS) comprising the latter products and adding a carbon capture process. The research investigates the potential for achieving net-negative carbon emissions by capturing CO 2 from two sources: the highly pure stream from ethanol fermentation and the flue gas from the bagasse-fired CHP plant. The integrated model focuses on maximizing the use of CO 2 neutral bagasse and optimizing the energy balance. Techno-economic (TEA) and life cycle analysis (LCA) were conducted to assess system performance. The results indicate that the minimal total CCS cost is achieved using the internal steam generated from sugarcane bagasse. This scenario corresponds to a 22% CO 2 capture rate, with total and CCS costs of 86.8 and 73.9 US$/ton CO 2 , respectively. To achieve a higher CO 2 capture rate, external energy input (steam and/or power) is required. However, this necessity reduces the cost-competitiveness of the BECCS process, particularly if the external energy is sourced from conventional fossil fuels. Ultimately, the integration of the BECCS system significantly reduces the overall environmental impacts associated with the production of bioethanol, energy, and sugar; especially with key indicators such as Global Warming Potential (GWP100), human toxicit potential (HTP) y, and specific aquatic ecotoxicity potential (SAEP).

title: Dual-phase nanoconfinement effects: Vanadium-MOF derived nanoporous carbon-coated V2O3 nanorods as multifunctional additives for advanced Mg-based hydrogen storage
A bi-level optimization framework for capacity configuration of high-penetration renewable energy systems enhanced by pumped storage
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy, driven by the China’s carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, has become an inevitable trend in modern power systems, yet its inherent stochasticity and volatility challenge system stability and economic operation. This study takes a prefecture-level city in East China (thermal 42.1%, wind 23.6%, photovoltaic 34.3%) as a case and develops a capacity configuration optimization model for a thermal–wind–photovoltaic–pumped storage integrated system (TWPIS). Using wind, photovoltaic, and load data from 2019, the Synchronous Backward Reduction (SBR) algorithm generates 27 typical scenarios to characterize source–load uncertainty. A bi-level optimization framework is then established: the outer level optimizes renewable capacity using the Multi-Objective Multi-Verse Optimizer (MOMVO), while the inner level solves a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) operational model via CPLEX combined with the ε-constraint method. The optimal configuration is selected from the Pareto frontier through an entropy-weighted TOPSIS approach. Results show that introducing pumped storage reduces the required wind and photovoltaic capacities from 3,978 MW and 2,274 MW to 2,700 MW and 1,110 MW, respectively. Through peak-shaving and valley-filling, wind and photovoltaic curtailment rates drop from over 20% and 50% to below 6%, while the total operating cost decreases by approximately 47% on average. Annual time-series simulation further confirms that the system operates efficiently and stably for more than 75% of the time. The findings demonstrate that pumped storage plays a critical role in enhancing flexibility, promoting renewable integration, and ensuring economic operation of high-renewable power systems.

Numerical investigations of the thermal performance of a novel groundwater – filled ground heat exchanger design
abstract: Ground heat exchangers are key components of shallow geothermal systems, including ground-coupled heat pumps and underground thermal energy storage systems. Reducing their installation costs through innovative designs remains a major challenge. In this study, the thermal performance of a Novel groundwater-filled Ground Heat Exchanger (NGHE) designed to promote thermally induced natural convection is investigated. The system incorporates truncated conical heat exchange plates, which increase the effective heat transfer surface area per unit depth and enhance thermally induced convective flow. A numerical model is developed and validated using experimental data to assess the behavior of this new design at shallow subsurface installation depths (i.e. 3–9 m below basement level). Three installation configurations have been proposed and analyzed. A comprehensive set of simulations is carried out to quantify the influence of key design parameters, installation geometry, and subsurface hydrogeological conditions. The metropolitan area of Bari (Italy) is used as a climate and hydrogeological framework. Results indicate that the novel ground heat exchanger is more efficient than the Conventional Ground Heat Exchanger (CGHE) design under a wide range of installation configurations, hydrogeological conditions, and operating modes. These findings suggest that the proposed heat exchanger could enable more compact and cost-effective shallow geothermal systems.

Hybrid algorithm for medium-term photovoltaic power prediction. Two-stage clustering-CNN-BiLSTM-Attention: Case study Lima (Peru)
abstract: The dimensioning of a solar plant requires historical information on seasonal meteorological variability where it will be installed. To ensure efficient photovoltaic (PV) energy production, accurate predictions that recognize variability are necessary. There are various hybrid prediction models without clear verification of the quality of clustering. Current PV prediction models have architectures with more accurate results but with a significant increase in computational time. A novel hybrid model is proposed that uses real historical data with a two-stage clustering process: physical-deterministic clustering for climatic seasons and clustering with the K-Medoids method to segment overcast and clear days, the results of which are incorporated into the CNN-BiLSTM-Attention prediction model trained on the residual over the cluster-mean baseline, allowing competitive results to be obtained over time horizons of 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, and 21 days. The clustering quality is supported by the joint optimization of three indices: Silhouette Score (SS) between 0.6698 and 0.8616, Calinski-Harabasz (CHI) up to 655.86, and Davies–Bouldin (DBI) as low as 0.4320, identifying 𝐾 ∗ = 2 as optimal across all four seasons. The proposed model attains 𝑅 2 between 0.8330 and 0.8453, RMSE between 0.1585 and 0.1627 kW, and MAE between 0.1156 and 0.1171 kW across the six horizons evaluated under stratified 7-daily split, 5-fold expanding-window cross-validation, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and Diebold–Mariano testing. During the 2023–2024 Coastal El Niño event, the model performs ＋2.6% better in 𝑅 2 than under normal conditions (0.8721 vs. 0.8498), demonstrating the robustness of two-stage clustering under anomalous climatic regimes.

Multidisciplinary design optimization for wave-driven desalination systems
abstract: Wave-driven desalination systems are an innovative solution to the global freshwater crisis, leveraging the complementary characteristics of seawater reverse osmosis and wave energy converters. However, the high costs of this system pose a significant barrier to widespread adoption. Optimization can help these systems reach a more competitive levelized cost of water, but the highly coupled nature of the system necessitates a multidisciplinary design optimization approach. This paper presents a holistic, multidisciplinary design optimization framework for wave-driven desalination system design, integrating models for wave energy converter hydrodynamics, power take-off transmission, seawater reverse osmosis constraints, and economic analysis. This study demonstrates the impact of multidisciplinary design optimization for wave-driven desalination systems, resulting in a 69.5% reduction in levelized cost of water within this modeling framework compared to a nominal design. We demonstrate that multidisciplinary design optimization outperforms two different sequential design approaches, yielding lower levelized costs of water and substantially different optimal designs. The multidisciplinary design optimization results suggest major design changes compared to designs found in the literature. Notably, smaller wave energy converters and larger pistons, along with smaller accumulators and larger seawater reverse osmosis plant installations, are preferred within this modeling framework. These design trends are consistent across a range of sea states, suggesting potential generalizability beyond a single location. This study demonstrates the importance of holistic modeling and co-design for wave-driven desalination systems and establishes an effective optimization framework for future studies to build upon.

Beyond the IRENA baseline: Mapping end-of-life photovoltaic waste flows across EU-27 using Weibull lifetime distributions screened against Eurostat data and updated efficiency scenarios
abstract: As the European Union accelerates photovoltaic deployment to achieve the milestones outlined in the 2025 National Energy and Climate Plans, accurate waste forecasting emerges as a significant challenge for the circular economy. This study re-evaluates EU-27 PV waste projections through 2050, comparing theoretical models with available empirical Eurostat collection data. Findings indicate that the standard IRENA Regular Loss model systematically underestimates waste generation, resulting in collection rates that exceed 200%. A new scenario, RL NEW , is proposed, featuring a revised Weibull parameterization and an updated time-variable mass-to-capacity transformation function. This alternative baseline scenario, screened for consistency against Eurostat aggregate data, forecasts cumulative 2025 waste volumes that are 214% higher than previous estimates. For the first time, projections are disaggregated by application, revealing a rooftop-dominated market in which 60% of waste necessitates decentralized logistics. The analysis identifies a bifurcated challenge: established operators should expand capacity to manage 65% of the European Union’s waste, while rapidly growing markets encounter surges up to 12,000-fold. Additionally, the Collection Difficulty Index is introduced to quantify the logistical impact of waste stream fragmentation, identifying a "Logistical Pivot" around 2030 when utility-scale surges begin to alleviate the logistical burden of decentralized systems. This framework provides quantitative information that can be used for cross-border logistics and recycling capacity planning.

Tunable all-day thermoelectric generator driven by solar heating and radiative cooling
abstract: The complementary utilization of solar heating and radiative cooling offers a promising approach for all-day thermoelectric energy harvesting. In this work, a tunable all-day thermoelectric generator (TAD-TEG) integrating a solar absorber, an optical filter, an IST-based phase-change radiative cooler, and a thermoelectric generator is proposed, and its optical, thermal, and power-generation performance is numerically investigated using a steady-state coupled thermal–electrical model. The optimized solar absorber achieves an AM1.5-weighted solar absorptance of 0.961, while the assembled cold-side system exhibits an emissivity of 0.980 in the 8–13 μm atmospheric window in the cooling-mode “on” state and 0.007 in the “off” state, enabling pronounced radiative modulation. Under representative baseline environmental conditions, the average power densities in the “on” state reach 12.80 W/m 2 during the daytime and 0.114 W/m 2 at night, markedly higher than the corresponding values of 7.45 and 0.011 W/m 2 in the “off” state. The corresponding 24-h electrical energy yields are 167.66 and 96.99 Wh/m 2 , respectively, indicating that radiative-state switching can effectively regulate the all-day thermoelectric output. Further analysis shows that the system exhibits tunable thermoelectric responses under different environmental conditions and TEG parameters, together with favorable power-generation performance across different seasons and geographical locations. These results indicate that the proposed TAD-TEG enables the synergistic utilization of solar heating and radiative cooling through cold-side radiative modulation, providing a promising tunable strategy for all-day thermoelectric energy harvesting under diverse climatic conditions.

Comparative assessment of long-term methodologies for building-integrated photovoltaic façade energy yield estimation
abstract: ABSTRACT Modelling energy yield of building-integrated photovoltaics requires reliable long-term energy output predictions that match actual generation to encourage its adoption and guarantee cost-effectiveness. This paper evaluates the performance of a Typical Meteorological Year in building-integrated photovoltaic simulations across three façade orientations (east, south and west), and proposes two alternative strategies that improve energy output predictions: a Typical Energy Year based on simulations over 19 years and the Finkelstein-Schafer statistic, and a typical meteorological year specifically designed for building-integrated photovoltaic systems based on the plane-of-array irradiance—which better relates to the tilted positioning of photovoltaic modules on building envelopes—and custom weighting factors for the meteorological variables that are adjusted for each specific case study. Simulation results show good behaviour of both proposed strategies, which provide highly accurate annual energy yield estimations overall. The reliability of the existing Typical Meteorological Year varies with array orientation, boundary conditions and annual variability, suggesting that it requires case-specific analysis to assess suitability. The three methodologies are mutually complementary, and the paper provides guidance towards what strategy is preferable based on key decision aspects, marking a step forward towards better accuracy in building-integrated photovoltaic performance simulations and supporting its implementation in architectural projects.

title: Construction of the combustion mechanism for biodiesel-n-butanol dual-fuel systems and analysis of nitrogen oxides formation pathways
Field testing of an axial-flow marine current turbine with passive adaptive blades
abstract: For axial-flow turbines, passive adaptive blades designed to passively feather in response to increasing thrust have the potential to decrease peak loads without the need for active pitch mechanisms, which come at the cost of additional failure modes and system complexity. In this study, we tested a 1-meter diameter axial-flow turbine in open water with two sets of composite blades: one blade set with a bend-twist coupling and a second, neutral blade set with no bend-twist coupling for comparison. Both blade sets were tested over a range of tip-speed ratios from 2 to 9, inflow speeds from 0.9 to 1.8 m/s, and yaw angles of 0, 15, and 25 degrees. The neutral blades were also tested over a range of preset blade pitch angles from −3 to 20 degrees. Testing over this wide range of operating conditions allowed us to assess the benefits of passive adaptive blades under low-frequency flow fluctuations in above-rated flow speeds (like those experienced during a tidal cycle) as well as cyclic, once-per-revolution loading. The bend-twist coupled blades were observed to achieve the same peak power coefficient as the neutral blades with a 7% reduction in thrust when operating at peak efficiency, and up to a 15% reduction in thrust at high tip-speed ratios. Interpolating across the experimental data, we simulated multiple off-design control strategies which estimate even greater load reduction potential. Further comparisons under yawed inflow are also discussed.

title: Multi-physics coupling simulation of biomass chemical looping gasification (CLG) for H2 production and CO2 mitigation
Improving solar irradiance estimates for PV production in Ireland using Bayesian spatio-temporal modelling with open-source data
abstract: Accurate solar irradiance estimation is essential for reliable modelling of solar photovoltaic(PV) power production. In Ireland’s mid-to-high latitude maritime climate, solar estimation is shaped by seasonal variation, low winter sun angles, frequent cloud variability, sparse ground-based measurements and discrepancies among satellite products, making solar irradiance dataset selection challenging. We develop a Bayesian spatio-temporal framework for country-specific solar irradiance estimates across Ireland using openly available data. The model produces hourly and sub-hourly estimates with full uncertainty quantification, and is designed to support site evaluation and near-real-time applications. Cross-validation demonstrates statistically robust performance across temporal resolutions with hourly showing highest precision whereas sub-hourly encounters higher errors but improved uncertainty quantification. We compare with reanalysis data(ERA5), nearest-station interpolation and satellite-based products(CAMS). Our model outperforms ERA5 for hourly resolutions, reducing RMSE from 82 W/m² to 36 W/m² highlighting the limitations of coarse-resolution global reanalysis products in Ireland’s persistently cloudy climate. We also present the first evaluation of CAMS in an Irish context. For hourly irradiance, CAMS outperforms ERA5; however, our model further reduces RMSE(40 W/m² vs 35 W/m²). For PV power estimation, our framework remains competitive with CAMS while providing uncertainty unavailable for CAMS or ERA5. Our framework's practical value is demonstrated through comparisons with PV power output from residential, industrial and utility sites in Ireland, showing strong agreement with observed generation and providing an open-source irradiance dataset with full uncertainty quantification for high resolution solar resource assessment and improved estimation of PV system losses(e.g.clipping).

title: Study on operational characteristics and performance prediction of a water-cooled photovoltaic and thermal system
Atmospheric regime clustering based on aerosol optical depth and cloud fraction for the improvement of 1-minute direct and diffuse solar irradiance separation
Biomethane-driven SOFC vehicles: Dual role in emission reduction and renewable energy production
abstract: : Fossil fuel combustion in road transport significantly contributes to greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution, necessitating sustainable alternatives. Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCs) fueled by biomethane offer a viable decarbonization pathway, leveraging existing biofuel infrastructure and enabling internal fuel reforming. This study employs an Integrated Assessment Model to assess the environmental benefits of introducing a biomethane-powered SOFC fleet. Additionally, this study explores the potential of SOFC vehicles to operate as prosumers, generating surplus energy to the grid during idle periods, thereby enhancing renewable energy integration. The impact assessment is analyzed in terms of CO 2-eq emission reduction and air quality benefits. The scenario focuses on the emissions variation affected by the substitution of traditional light-duty vehicles with SOFC vehicles, the replacement of energy produced by non-renewable sources with the energy produced by the fleet, and the influence of the biomethane production process (including biomethane production sites and feedstock waste management). The case study is the Lombardy region in Northern Italy, characterized by elevated pollution levels. Results indicate that replacing conventional vehicles with SOFCs can reduce GHG, NOx, and NH 3 emissions substantially, leading to measurable air quality improvements and decreased fossil fuel dependence in transport and energy sectors.

title: How do solar energy landscapes transform geography? Synergistic multi-objective optimization for robust PV and CSP planning in island regions
Assessment of waste-energy-hydrogen technologies as a pathway to sustainable transportation in Gaza Strip, Palestine
Design of a Francis turbine for wider range of head and power via runner inlet and outlet optimization
Who gets the jobs? Embedding regional employment equity in energy system planning
abstract: The energy transition can create substantial employment, yet its spatial distribution can reinforce territorial inequalities. Most energy planning studies compute employment ex post from predefined pathways, so distributive objectives cannot influence investment or operation and the marginal cost of redistribution remains unobservable. This study proposes a novel methodology to evaluate territorial employment distributive policies within energy system optimization by making regional direct employment endogenous and subject to distributive constraints. We extend the multizonal H2RES model by linking region- and technology-specific employment factors to annual capacity decisions and requiring each region to reach a minimum share of national net direct employment. Employment thus becomes a policy constraint that shapes investment siting, technology choice, and system operation, while revealing marginal redistribution costs through shadow prices. Applied to Chile’s National Electric System through 2050 across seven equity levels, the framework reshapes decarbonization pathways, altering renewable siting, technology mix, and flexibility use. Stronger equity raises system costs up to 3.95%, driven by higher wind investment and solar relocation toward lower-yield regions, while net direct employment rises up to 27% under maximum equity. Marginal costs show that Norte Chico and Centro are most costly, Sur binds only at high equity, and Norte Grande never binds.

title: Experimental investigation of coupled heat and mass transfer in a solar humidification–dehumidification desalination system
Multiscale assessment of market concentration and inequality in the global wood pellet trade: Implications for the bioenergy transition
abstract: Densified biomass fuels, particularly wood pellets have emerged as strategic assets in the global low-carbon energy transition. This study conducts a multiscale assessment of spatial concentration and inequality in wood pellet production and consumption from 2012 to 2022 using FAO data and five structural indicators: Concentration Ratios (CR k ), Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI), Theil Entropy Index (E), Gini Coefficient (G), and Hall–Tideman Index (HTI). Results reveal significant market expansion, especially in Europe and East Asia, alongside declining production concentration. While CR k and HHI suggest growing diversification, G and HTI indicate persistent inequalities, particularly in national-level consumption. Brazil stands out with the highest growth rate among major producers. These findings offer robust evidence to guide renewable energy policies, promote fair international trade, and foster a more inclusive global bioeconomy.

Sobol-based global sensitivity analysis of D-shaped bluff body piezoelectric energy harvesters using SVM surrogate model
abstract: To address the unclear parameter regulation mechanism of D-shaped bluff body piezoelectric micro wind energy harvesters caused by strong geometric-system parameter coupling and pronounced nonlinearity, this study develops a synergistic parameter analysis framework combining Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Sobol global sensitivity analysis to investigate the effects and synergistic mechanisms of wind speed, aspect ratio, mass damping ratio and system stiffness on amplitude ratio.540 sets of full-condition vibration response data were obtained via three-factor three-level orthogonal tests and continuous wind speed scanning. An SVM surrogate model with radial basis function kernel was established, achieving a test set coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9655, meeting high-precision analysis requirements. Global sensitivity analysis shows that wind speed dominates amplitude ratio across all conditions with a total effect index of 59.00%, followed by aspect ratio (19.05%), stiffness (10.33%) and mass damping ratio (8.92%). Mass damping ratio exhibits strong interaction effects, while aspect ratio acts almost independently. Dominant parameters evolve significantly with wind speed: mass damping ratio dominates at low speeds, stiffness at medium speeds, and both aspect ratio and stiffness at high speeds. This study reveals the multi-parameter mechanism under coupled vortex-induced vibration (VIV) and galloping in D-shaped bluff bodies, providing an efficient analytical tool and theoretical support for parameter matching and optimal design of micro wind energy devices.

Participation assessment of diverse multi-energy microgrids in integrated power–water distribution systems considering outages
Impact of circumsolar irradiance and aerosol optical depth on CAMS surface solar irradiance estimates
abstract: The global horizontal irradiance is a main variable in the integration of solar energy systems in electricity grids, and in climate and weather studies. The physical model McClear is the clear-sky module for the all-sky irradiance retrievals from the CAMS Radiation Service. Validations of McClear against high-quality in situ measurements reveal very accurate global horizontal irradiance estimates with negligible bias. Albeit still good, the beam and diffuse irradiance components exhibit biases generally opposing each other. These biases are mainly attributed to the aerosol optical depth used as input to McClear, and the forward scattered circumsolar irradiance surrounding the solar disc which is not modelled by McClear but intercepted within the solid angle aperture of radiometers measuring beam irradiance (and blocked by those measuring diffuse irradiance). This study performs a global scale validation of a desert-based circumsolar correction, and evaluates the influence of this circumsolar correction and the aerosol optical depth on the beam and diffuse irradiance estimates from McClear. Circumsolar corrected retrievals are enhanced globally, especially for the diffuse component of McClear, with the standard deviation of deviations improving from 26.3 to 24.4%, the bias from 19.0 to 13.1%, and the correlation remaining constant at 0.837. Comparing ground measured and CAMS modelled aerosol optical depth, improvements are expected with further developments to the CAMS aerosol model.

Performance and robustness evaluation of retrofit and standard LiDAR-assisted control in wind turbines
abstract: LiDAR-assisted control has emerged as a promising approach to proactively mitigate turbine loads by exploiting upstream wind measurements. Standard LAC designs, however, typically require modifications to the existing controller architecture, such as injecting a feed-forward pitch signal to the actuator or embedding feed-forward pitch rates in the feedback loop. This work proposes a novel retrofit LiDAR-assisted control solution that can be implemented without prior knowledge or modification of the existing feedback controller. The retrofit strategy achieves feed-forward pitch action by perturbing the rotor speed measurement. A theoretical analysis establishes the equivalence between the proposed retrofit and standard methods in terms of closed-loop performance. This study presents a systematic performance and robustness analysis of standard and retrofit methods using sparse and dense LiDAR beam configurations. The sensitivity to LiDAR pre-filtering parameters, including buffer time and filter frequency, as well as retrofit-specific tuning parameters, is investigated. Simulation results show that, with appropriate tuning, standard and retrofit methods achieve comparable performance in reducing key turbine loads. Furthermore, robustness analysis demonstrates that retrofit design maintains satisfactory performance under tuning uncertainties. These findings provide practical guidelines for deploying retrofit solutions in operational turbines and highlight their potential to extend turbine lifetimes cost-effectively.

title: Energy potential and environmental benefits of hybrid floating photovoltaic systems on dams in Thailand
Renewable energy production forecasting based on fractional order polynomial sinusoidal driving grey prediction model
Shallow geothermal energy in the Canary Islands: Resource and technical potential for energy planning
abstract: This study presents an archipelago-wide assessment of shallow geothermal potential in the Canary Islands, integrating subsurface thermal properties, groundwater influence, and spatially explicit heating and cooling demand within an enhanced GIS-based application of the G.POT methodology. Ground thermal conductivity was estimated by accounting for lithology and groundwater depth, enabling differentiation between saturated and unsaturated conditions. A municipality-level comparison between aggregated thermal demand and shallow geothermal potential was performed to evaluate the extent to which local resources could offset climatization needs. Results indicate that cooling potential consistently exceeds heating potential across all islands, reaching up to 14 MWh per borehole per year, reflecting the cooling-dominated energy profile of this subtropical region. Thermal demand is highly concentrated in Tenerife and Gran Canaria, which together account for 67.7% of total climatization requirements. While municipal-scale results suggest a substantial technical resource, realistic deployment is strongly constrained by land availability. Urban case studies in Tenerife show that compact metropolitan areas can meet only 1.7% of cooling demand under realistic installation conditions, whereas more dispersed municipalities with greater surface availability can reach up to 17%. The study provides a spatial framework to support renewable cooling planning in volcanic and warm-climate island contexts.

title: Influences of copper foam geometrical parameters on the quenching behavior of premixed green H2-air venting flames
Robust planning for multi-path retrofits of coal-fired power plants considering biomass gasification co-firing
Real-time I–V curve scaling and MPP estimation through polynomial regression model for photovoltaic modules based on Gompertz functions
abstract: This paper proposes a simplified and computationally efficient method for scaling the current–voltage and estimating maximum power point characteristics of photovoltaic modules, specifically designed for real-time monitoring. The proposed approach firstly estimates the symmetrized and shifted Gompertz model under standard conditions. By considering other irradiance and temperature conditions, both short-circuit current and open-circuit voltage values are used to scale the current–voltage curve and, subsequently, the maximum power point value is then estimated by using a polynomial regression model, avoiding iterative and complex processes. A large-scale statistical analysis is performed using 130 monocrystalline silicon photovoltaic modules from 44 manufacturers, producing 4550 scaled current–voltage curves. The results showed that 99.51% of the polynomial regression maximum power point values differed by less than 1% from those calculated by the Gompertz model, and 100% remained within a 1.5% error margin. A case study using 1725 real operating points from a commercial photovoltaic plant further validated the model, providing an average energy deviation of less than 5.6% compared to real collected photovoltaic generation for 11 days. The computational time was significantly reduced from 14–212 s per current–voltage curve by using the iterative Gompertz method to lower than one second with the proposed approach under different current hardware platforms. These results confirm the feasibility of the method for low-resource, real-time applications, including embedded systems and micro-inverters. Future work will focus on integrating thermal dynamic behavior and extending the model for accurate energy forecasting under variable environmental conditions.

title: Carbon-responsibility-aware peer-to-peer trading mechanism for microgrids with heterogeneous energy
Seasonal resilient operation of a solar-based off-grid integrated energy system for plateau mining areas: A risk-averse IGDT approach
Assessment of photovoltaic energy potential over Italy from an ensemble of convection permitting climate models
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) energy production is crucial to achieve climate neutrality by 2050 and is tightly linked to climate variability and change. In particular, variations in the availability of surface solar radiation impact PV energy potential, while temperature and wind affect PV cell efficiency. Here, for the first time, we evaluate the ability of a 16-member km-scale convection-permitting climate model (CPMs) ensemble to reproduce PV energy potential over Italy. The assessment is conducted at station and national level using ERA5-land reanalysis dataset as reference. Driving climate variables are further evaluated against available high-resolution observations. The quality assessment of CPMs and ERA5-land data reveal an overestimation of downward shortwave radiation at the surface by CPMs (+6% in summer) and underestimation by similar amounts in ERA5-land compared to the high-resolution observational dataset. The 2m temperatures and 10 m wind speeds are slightly overestimated in CPMs as well by 1.24C and 0.54 m/s respectively. Based on this good agreement, the energy potential model previously validated with ERA5-land is applied to CPMs. The CPM ensemble shows realistic diurnal and seasonal cycles, but tends to overestimate PV potential relative to ERA5-land by up to +10 % at individual stations and +13 % at bidding zones, in particular due to the bias in radiation. Ensemble spread is 20% in summer, but significantly lower within model families. These findings support the use of CPM ensembles for climate change impact studies on solar resources, providing high resolution information to support adaptation strategies in power system planning at local scale.

Data-driven prognostic algorithm based on Bi-LSTM transformer model for proton exchange membrane fuel cell
abstract: The complex interaction of internal physical phenomena makes predicting the degradation of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) under dynamic operating conditions a critical but persistent challenge. To address this, the present work develops a hybrid model based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) layers with a multi-head self-attention mechanism to capture degradation dependencies across both short and long time-frames. When benchmarked against state-of-the-art architectures, including attention-based LSTM variants and the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT), the model achieves a reduction of up to 52.7% in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The model’s accuracy is confirmed across single-step, multi-step, and long-term forecasting scenarios, where it consistently maintains high predictive accuracy ( R 2 ≥ 0.998 ) for prediction horizons of up to 175 steps ahead. Furthermore, this high performance is achieved with notable data efficiency, requiring a training dataset of 300 h. These combined strengths in accuracy, long-term reliability, and data efficiency make the proposed Bi-LSTM Transformer an effective tool for predictive health management under dynamic load cycles.
